title: Complete public GovHub with Castor native operations and receiving

# Operate one saved GovHub project

## Initialize or reopen

Use separate absolute private directories for the editable workspace and supplied inputs. Do not put either inside the public source tree. The original CLI creates one named administrator and stores the password using the existing assessment engine. The default password prompt avoids placing a secret in command history; --password-env NAME can select an already configured private host environment value.

~~~sh
starforge govhub --python /absolute/existing/python3 cli \
  --workspace /private/govhub/project \
  --source-root /private/govhub/inputs \
  --username operator init --name "Site operations" --mode SUPPLIED
~~~

Use PILOT only for an explicitly authored commissioning cohort. The application does not treat example rows as customer observations.

Open the original application:

~~~sh
starforge govhub --python /absolute/existing/python3 serve \
  --workspace /private/govhub/project \
  --source-root /private/govhub/inputs --port 0
~~~

The server prints its actual loopback URL and workspace directory. Open that address and sign in with the retained account. The installed Applications entry takes the same existing workspace, input directory, optional Python executable and port. It starts the same original server; the application's own service lease owns its worker. Use Applications Stop before opening another server or CLI worker on that project.

A workspace already containing assessment.sqlite3 must be reopened rather than initialized again. The source-input directory is part of the saved project binding. Follow the original receiving relocation path when moving a private project; do not edit stored operation identities or fabricate a new workspace to bypass a pending command.

## Native source and operation flow

Create or reopen the environment's original provider profile. Provider paths are runtime bindings; the project/site/environment IDs and source revision identify the intended target. Each provider guide lists exact supported actions and required native tools. Credentials are supplied by the existing host's native session or environment-name references.

Retain the complete source first. Review the current source comparison and selected native capabilities. Create the original operation with its stable request key. An accepted provider workflow or activity remains the authoritative continuation; poll that same identity and observe its original retry deadline. A lost response is reconciled using the provider's explicit association controls. It does not authorize issuing the mutation again with a new request key.

The original command journal retains argv, cwd, stdout, stderr, file identities and pending native command state. If the host or process is interrupted, use its saved continuation and actual receiving-host paths. Keep the original source and operation records. Cancellation and native completion are distinct states.

The native provider snapshots and local source packages also have different meanings. Upsun snapshots cannot be downloaded as source archives: its complete source arm receives actual Git, database dump and selected writable mounts. Pantheon, Skpr, Tugboat and the other adapters retain their native provider IDs and exact source semantics. Read the selected provider guide before choosing a recovery action.

For Castor, choose the actual existing task and verification task from the selected native context, with reviewed arguments and explicit JSON outcome checks. Source capture retains the original Git index and working files, selected Compose configuration, immutable Docker image identities and full image-save bytes. A successful process exit alone does not establish successful backup or restoration. Keep an uncertain process on its original command receipt; use the separate source receiving continuation for an interrupted independent Git reopen. The complete native and browser course is in CASTOR_RECEIVING.md.

## CLI operation and backup

Arguments after the launcher command are passed unchanged to the maintained programme. Obtain each full native syntax through:

~~~sh
starforge govhub cli --help
starforge govhub build --help
starforge govhub upsun-receive --help
starforge govhub castor-receive --help
starforge govhub pantheon-receive --help
starforge govhub static-releases --help
starforge govhub dnn --help
~~~

A named private JSON input can drive an original GovHub action:

~~~sh
starforge govhub cli --workspace /private/govhub/project \
  --source-root /private/govhub/inputs --username operator \
  call ACTION --input /private/govhub/request.json
~~~

Use the action and full actual input returned by the original interface; action names in the provider receiving courses are the authority. Native receiving programmes use the same saved queue rather than a second controller.

Create the full original private backup into a new absolute directory:

~~~sh
starforge govhub cli --workspace /private/govhub/project \
  --source-root /private/govhub/inputs --username operator \
  backup --destination /private/govhub/receiving-copy
~~~

Keep the original complete backup report and original source files. A backup containing an incomplete marker is pending receiving, not a finished delivery. The exact component receiving course carries its native artifacts, operation continuations and independently reopened project as described in RECEIVING.md.

## Actual product inspection

Open, use and LOOK at the exact outgoing product as its recipient would. Inspect the original saved project at the actual presentation width and relevant narrow width; view the real images you capture. Exercise the selected content/provider controls, populated and empty/error views, saved decisions, native continuation and downloadable results. Open every applicable report and usable archive content, then reopen the delivered project in a separate directory.

Source parsing, HTTP success, DOM counts and another worker's review are not substitutes for observed operation. Repair any clipped, unstyled, overflowing or unreadable output in the same maintained source. Keep this work focused on the actual remaining product risk; do not replace it with a broad test campaign.

If the selected runtime is unavailable, retain this complete source edition and pending original operation for its existing equipped owner and inspect that owner's actual rendered return. Do not claim a native provider action, account access or final customer acceptance from source review alone. Preserve the existing zero-spend policy: no hosted Actions, paid runner or new provider account is introduced by this product.

# GovHub site operations

GovHub is a local operating application for complete site source capture, reviewed content and release changes, native recovery and private project handover. It keeps original source bytes, provider/workflow identities, operator decisions, command output and complete editable workspace backups in one saved project.

## Open the installed product

Choose the **govhub** source selection in the existing Source Builds interface or use the repository's original distribution builder with --selection govhub. The contribution adds **Applications → GovHub site operations** and the **starforge govhub** command. The installed source contains the complete Python application and all provider, content, visitor, release and receiving components.

Use an existing POSIX host with Python 3.11 or later and SQLite support. The managed application uses the selected host's Python; it does not install or authenticate external providers. Node runs only the installed command/Applications integration. Drupal, PHP, Drush, Git and each provider's CLI or account remain explicit native inputs described by their own guide.

1. Read [OPERATING.md](OPERATING.md) and initialize a private workspace using the original CLI.
2. Open that same workspace and supplied-input directory through Applications or the original server command.
3. Select actual provider/environment/source identities and complete the existing review and native operation workflow.
4. Follow [RECEIVING.md](RECEIVING.md) to build the whole application, preserve the full private project and reopen it independently.

## Included operating areas

| --- | --- |
| Cutover and recovery | application/START_HERE.md and application/workspace/README.md |
| Drupal / Lagoon | application/workspace/NATIVE_SOURCES.md and LAGOON.md |

| Tugboat | application/workspace/TUGBOAT.md and TUGBOAT_RECEIVING.md |

| POTS / CircleCI deployment observations | application/workspace/pots/README.md and CAPTURE.md |

The public source projection retains complete implementation and third-party notices. Private outreach, case correspondence, host custody locators and completed private runtime receipts are excluded. Original public source references remain where they explain actual provider or commissioning semantics. A source package is separate from the private workspace backup, which deliberately retains the original accounts, supplied source and operation history.

This is source delivery. Native account acceptance, provider mutations and rendered product acceptance require the selected original receiving operation's actual outcomes.

# Complete application and private project receiving

## Source identity and package

The public product preserves the application's original relative layout under products/govhub/application. Its source manifest records every complete public postimage. The original private source packet remains separately retained by its original owner. Public adaptations remove private routing and commercial prose, parameterize commissioning inputs and refresh source locks; they do not import private accounts or runtime data.

Use an immutable public repository commit when making the source lock:

~~~sh
python3 products/govhub/application/workspace/build_application.py lock \
  --repository /absolute/merchant-checkout --revision ACTUAL_FULL_COMMIT \
  --output /private/APPLICATION_SOURCE.json

python3 products/govhub/application/workspace/build_application.py build \
  --source-root /absolute/merchant-checkout/products/govhub/application \
  --manifest /private/APPLICATION_SOURCE.json \
  --output /private/GovHub-Complete-Application.zip

python3 products/govhub/application/workspace/build_application.py verify \
  /private/GovHub-Complete-Application.zip --expected-sha256 ACTUAL_WHOLE_ZIP_SHA256
~~~

The build reads every selected original Git source object, verifies bytes and hashes, streams the complete archive and independently reopens all members. The package opens as govhub-operations/ with its exact APPLICATION_SOURCE.json and PACKAGE.json. It includes every provider, shared engine, UI, receiver, native source contract and license. The source boundary rejects case-assets/ in both generated and supplied manifests. The optional --terminus-phar takes the exact existing original release; it does not download or replace a native CI runtime.

The generated APPLICATION_SOURCE.json is excluded from its own source inventory. Its source_commit identifies the complete source edition used to produce it. The public DNN engine lock likewise names exact current engine member bytes; its own lock is not a recursively hashed engine member.

## Whole saved project

Select the original saved workspace and its full supplied-input directory. Read the pending operations before closing its current server/worker. Retain source artifacts and native operation journals, including incomplete requests and actual provider acceptance. Export the selected source-inclusive handover and full workspace backup through the original application.

Reopen the copied workspace with the received application's own assessment core and the original account. Verify that the original source IDs, content decisions, provider/workflow or activity IDs and selected native release are retained. The component receiver performs its independent process and application ZIP receiving where documented. Keep all outputs and the full manifest; a list of archive URLs is not the project.

Provider recovery requires the destination host's explicitly selected current runtime paths and existing authorized account. A complete source build and local browser reopen can proceed before that provider input is available. Preserve an accepted original operation and its native receipt; a different physical host is not permission to select a different business target.

## Native courses

- Pantheon: application/workspace/pantheon_receive.py and PANTHEON_RECEIVING.md carry original PHAR/plugin setup, provider binding and full application/workspace reopen.
- Skpr: skpr_receive.py and SKPR.md retain actual native environment, source and complete restic receiving.
- Tugboat: tugboat_receive.py and TUGBOAT_RECEIVING.md retain original project/repository/preview and asynchronous job identity.
- Upsun: upsun_receive.py and UPSUN_RECEIVING.md carry the actual selected course, complete source archive, Git/index/worktree reopen, whole project and cold application reopen.
- Castor: castor_receive.py and CASTOR_RECEIVING.md carry selected original task/verification results, full Git/index/dirty source and image archives, hash-bound backup inputs, independent source reconstruction, a frozen original operation cohort, complete private project and cold reopen. native/castor/browser_receive.cjs opens that same saved project, retains actual wide/narrow images, checks real controls and complete downloads, and requires visual inspection of the returned images.
- Content: content_consolidation/NATIVE_SITE.md and content_packages/native_receiving/OPERATE.md describe complete native graph receiving, correction, deliberate isolated interruption and original import continuation.
- Tome: static_releases/TOME_RECEIVING.md and PORTABLE_RECEIVING.md cover complete native generation, publication, rollback, browser receiving and full local private handover.
- DNN: dnn_maintenance/RECEIVING.md covers the native Windows/IIS/SQL host and full private project restoration; public source does not discover an unrelated commercial case.

All example site, account, source and image selections must be replaced with the original actual receiving inputs. The selected commissioning namespaces are isolated exercises; a production account or customer approval is never implied.

## Portable Tome source selection

The whole portable receiver now takes --source-selection with a private JSON binding of the selected application ZIP/counts/manifest, actual full source commit, original runtime receiver, native/browser programme pins, Tome archive and site administrator email. It verifies complete source bodies before importing helpers. The same input is retained across interruption and resumption.

It returns complete local handover file identities by default. Both --delivery-programme and --library-helpers may select an already authorized original publisher; their full exact source pins belong in the same private selection. Existing unfinished publication remains with that original adapter. There is no hard-coded private Library identity, internal Slack route or implicit new upload destination in the public course.

## Final rendered and attachment receiving

Run the exact outgoing application. Open the same saved project at wide and narrow widths, view the actual captured images, use the important controls and download every selected result. Open the complete HTML/PDF/report pages and usable archive contents. Reopen the original private workspace independently and continue an actual retained operation only when its original inputs authorize it.

Record actual native stdout/stderr, source and artifact hashes, receiving project identity and observed rendered results in the existing operation. Fix concrete issues before marking delivery complete. Source publication is not native or rendered acceptance. If execution is unavailable, preserve the same complete source and accepted operation for its current equipped owner; no replacement dispatcher, account, hosted Actions run or paid runtime is created.

# GovHub site operations

GovHub is a local multi-site operating workspace for source capture, review, migration, release, recovery and complete project receiving. It retains original inputs, native commands and provider operations, editable decisions, reports and full workspace backups. All provider actions require the operator's existing selected account, environment and authorization.

Start with [START_HERE.md](START_HERE.md) and the [workspace guide](workspace/README.md). The enclosing [installed product guide](../README.md) explains the public source selection and Applications entry.

The complete source includes Drupal/Drush, Lagoon, Pantheon/Terminus, Skpr, Tugboat and Upsun providers; native POTS/CircleCI source capture; content consolidation and packages; editorial planning; visitor journeys; Tome static release/recovery; and the DNN maintenance desk. Their existing source, operation and receiving semantics are preserved.

## Reconcile supplied cutover exports

Python 3.10 or later runs the original cutover auditor using the standard library:

~~~sh
python3 cutover.py --before /private/incumbent.csv --after /private/candidate.csv --out /private/evidence --min-agencies 4
~~~

Choose the minimum cohort from the actual authorized inventory. Required columns are agency_id, canonical_url, export_sha256, backup_sha256, route_count and observed_http_status. Missing agencies, duplicates, invalid inputs, changed digests, route or URL drift and non-2xx responses remain visible. The optional approvals CSV binds each approved change to exact before/after values, a reviewer and a reason. An approval does not waive missing agencies or failed HTTP observations.

The supplied *.example.csv files are illustrative commissioning inputs. Real receiving requires original site exports, a native recovery exercise and the operator's reviewed acceptance criteria. The source application alone is not a security, accessibility or platform-compliance attestation.

## Source and private project custody

The application source has an Apache-2.0 license; included original provider contracts and third-party files retain their own notices. Public source excludes private customer cases, account values and editable runtime workspaces. Source packaging rejects case-assets/. Private project backups deliberately retain their original accounts, inputs and operation history and must stay in the selected private receiving custody.

# GovHub operations — start and receive

This package contains the complete retained cutover application, the unchanged original cutover comparator, the content consolidation and visitor journey products, their native Drupal receiving components, and the Drush, Acquia, Lagoon and Pantheon provider integrations. The source lock identifies every original file and its exact revision.

## Open the application

Use Linux and Python 3.11 or later. The application uses the Python standard library, SQLite and local files. Native providers run with their existing supported tools and account context. Keep the supplied directory structure together: workspace/server.py imports the original parent cutover.py and the included assessment core.

Extract the complete ZIP into a new application directory. Change into its govhub-operations folder. Create separate private directories for the operating workspace and incoming source files. Use the existing staff account when receiving an established workspace.

For a new operating workspace, run:

    python3 workspace/cli.py --workspace /absolute/private/govhub-workspace \
      --source-root /absolute/private/govhub-incoming --username operator \
      init --name "GovHub operations" --mode SUPPLIED

The original application asks for the new staff password in the terminal. Start its browser service on loopback:

    python3 workspace/server.py --workspace /absolute/private/govhub-workspace \
      --source-root /absolute/private/govhub-incoming --port 8792

Open http://127.0.0.1:8792 and use the retained staff account. The full operating guide is workspace/README.md. DOMAIN.md explains the inventory, native operations and original comparison workflow. NATIVE_SOURCES.md gives the native acquisition and receiving contracts. The original examples in the package root are clearly named example CSVs and remain separate from imported operating inventories.

For a terminal-only service, run the same durable queue:

    python3 workspace/cli.py --workspace /absolute/private/govhub-workspace \
      --source-root /absolute/private/govhub-incoming --username operator \
      worker --until-idle

The CLI retains the worker while an accepted original provider workflow is pollable, including a scheduled next poll. It returns when the queue settles or a saved operation requires its actual observation, original provider ID or other operator input. Its JSON result names the saved operations.

## Receive an established operation

Open the existing editable workspace backup through the application's receiving-copy workflow. Retain the complete original database, source files, command outputs and native operation directory. The receiving APIs preserve the original family and operation IDs, revisions, selected sources, approval history and native workflow continuation.

Use the receiving guide's exact workspace and source-store arguments. A private directory may move during receiving; the original command and request/receipt files follow the application’s private custody relocation. The configured business target remains the selected native site and environment.

Reopen the received workspace first and inspect its retained operations. Continue the same original provider workflow using its saved native ID or durable bridge receipt. Read the actual provider result and attach the observed restored inventory through the normal operating form. Export the completed handover and the editable workspace backup from the same application.

The content and visitor products retain their original receiving guides under workspace/content_consolidation and workspace/visitor_journeys. The package includes these whole namespaces so their source intake, native Drupal delivery and staff workflows remain available after receiving.

## Build a complete application release

The package includes workspace/build_application.py. It performs three distinct operations: retain an immutable source lock from Git, build the full ZIP from those exact files, and reopen a delivered ZIP to verify its members. It uses only Python's standard library and native Git for the lock command. Build and verify use the received source files and need no network access.

From an existing repository checkout, retain the full application source at the final composed commit:

    python3 products/govhub/application/workspace/build_application.py lock \
      --repository /absolute/commons --revision FULL_40_CHARACTER_COMMIT \
      --output /absolute/release/APPLICATION_SOURCE.json

The lock reads every tracked source member under products/govhub/application from that commit through one native Git object batch. Existing generated source/package indexes and the optional runtime PHAR have their own package slots. The source lock requires all native provider, bridge, receiver, content, visitor, core, UI and licensing dependencies.

Place the exact locked source in one application directory, preserving relative paths. Then build the original release:

    python3 /absolute/application/workspace/build_application.py build \
      --source-root /absolute/application \
      --manifest /absolute/release/APPLICATION_SOURCE.json \
      --terminus-phar /absolute/native/terminus-4.3.3.phar \
      --output /absolute/release/govhub-operations.zip

Omit --terminus-phar when the receiver will use its existing native installation. Every output path is create-only. Use a new filename for an updated source lock or application edition.

During the build, each file streams from its opened source into the ZIP and is checked against both its original Git blob and its SHA-256. The builder retains modes, original licenses, the full source lock and a package index. It reopens the completed ZIP and checks every member before publishing the final filename.

Verify a received ZIP using the original whole-file SHA-256 from its delivery:

    python3 workspace/build_application.py verify /absolute/received/govhub-operations.zip \
      --expected-sha256 ORIGINAL_64_CHARACTER_ZIP_SHA256

The result reports the complete ZIP bytes and SHA-256, original source commit, source member count and whether the pinned Terminus PHAR is included. The included source lock is a readable file map; the independently delivered whole-ZIP hash identifies the selected delivery.

# Native Castor release and recovery in GovHub

This provider connects the existing GovHub project, environment, reviewed plan,
operation journal and complete handover to an application's **existing Castor
tasks**. Castor performs the work. GovHub preserves the selected native source,
task definition, context, argument tokens, original process receipt, files and
verification results.

The selected project can use an installed Castor executable, a PHAR with an
explicit PHP launcher, or its own repacked executable. This integration does
not replace its task implementation or create a CI workflow. An article's
example application, registry, task names and credentials are never defaults.

## Authoritative source

The implemented CLI contract was read from JoliCode Castor **v1.8.1**, original
commit **058feddafd0b977eebf33364d02cd553ae26854a**, published September 21, 2026.
The original release metadata, native tag/tree response, selected complete
source files and MIT license are retained in native/castor/. The source index
records every original Git blob and UTF-8 identity.

Primary references:

- https://github.com/jolicode/castor/tree/058feddafd0b977eebf33364d02cd553ae26854a
- https://github.com/jolicode/castor/releases/tag/v1.8.1
- https://castor.jolicode.com/
- https://jolicode.com/blog/deploiement-on-premise-partie-2-castor-a-la-rescousse

The selected upstream Composer source requires PHP **8.4 or later**. The
previous optional PHP 8.3 Drupal closure is not a compatible launcher for this
release. Use the actual compatible launcher or the application's selected
complete static executable. Its version and full executable hash are
observed and retained; no automatic self-update or dependency substitution
occurs.

Castor's actual Kernel deliberately selects an empty context for its general
list command. The provider receives that full catalogue, then receives
native help for each selected application task in its **explicit context**.
A missing context or mismatched native task stops before application-task
dispatch. A repacked application may use another application name/version;
the actual installed tool and embedded source remain authoritative.

## Original operating model

Keep the selected application source tree and GovHub's private receiving
workspace in **separate directories**. Full source receiving must not ingest
its own newly created journals, images or archives. The provider rejects a
Session output directory inside the selected source tree.

One original GovHub environment owns:

- its existing deployment identity;
- its exact Docker context and Compose project;
- the ordered original Compose files;
- the selected Castor root and context;
- the full native source commit and actual working tree;
- the task and its exact arguments;
- the full backup/release/input/output selection and native verification.

Use the existing POSIX/Linux or WSL GovHub native Session host with its real Docker context. This provider preserves its process-group, filesystem and native lock behavior; a Windows Castor release asset alone does not establish Windows support for the surrounding GovHub runner.

Only the actual host executable paths and source directory are runtime
bindings. They cannot change the original deployment, Docker context,
Compose project, task selection, arguments, expected results, source commit,
or chosen recovery inputs.

A preview must target an existing GovHub environment whose purpose is
Candidate or Rehearsal. Rehearsal, Cutover and Rollback keep the existing
GovHub plan/source/review admission. Cutover still requires the original
passing comparison and explicit approving review. A selected task may
perform several native steps internally; its actual application source
defines those steps.

## Profile fields

All structured selections are explicit JSON text in the existing profile
form. Paths below are ordinary project-relative paths unless a native host
path is explicitly stated. Declared output paths and recovery inputs cannot
follow symlinks.

| --- | --- |
| source_kind | castor |

| castor_path | Actual installed Castor, repacked PHAR, or static executable |
| php_path | Explicit compatible PHP executable when launching a PHAR |

| castor_context | Actual selected named context; empty only if there are no named contexts |

| verify_task_name | Selected existing native verification task |
| verify_args_json | Exact native verification argument tokens |

| verify_output_path | Actual verification JSON file when verify_source is file |

The following are **shape examples**, not observed customer source:

    compose_files_json:
    ["compose.yaml","compose.production.yaml"]

    task_outputs_json:
    [
      {"path":"retained/database.sql","role":"database","kind":"file"},
      {"path":"retained/uploads","role":"files","kind":"directory"}
    ]

    [

Use the application's real file names, report shape, expected values and
task arguments. These examples are deliberately not executable defaults.
The provider does not synthesize a successful backup report or invent a
database consistency guarantee.

Every exact task token travels as an argv element through the existing
Session command runner. It is not interpreted by a shell. Task arguments
cannot override the bound Castor root or context, nor force another remote
import selection. Secret values belong in the original application's private
configuration or native credential storage, not argv or report labels.

## Capability and first Capture

Inspect the existing profile through GovHub's normal capability action.
The result includes full original task rows/help, observed version, source
head, selected files, native engine, Compose configuration and actual
containers/images. The local capability inspection is read-only orchestration
of native inspection commands; original application boot/context hooks still
run according to the selected Castor source.

The complete Capture does the following in the original receiving Session:

1. Receives native Git HEAD, index, tracked and untracked file identities,
   complete nested submodule worktree identities, and native task/tool output.
2. Receives Docker engine identity, complete selected Compose configuration,
   actual containers and images, original release files and declared outputs.
3. Passes that original selection to the complete source helper. A first
   capture without source_revision uses the actual observed full commit.
4. Receives source/Git/project, executable, selected image archives, declared
   original files and complete command outputs through the helper's verified
   archive.
5. Reads the same selected source/engine/configuration again. A changed
   original binding is retained as an incomplete operation rather than
   silently producing a mixed accepted source.

Task lists, native stdout/stderr and Compose configuration are private
source. Complete configuration can contain sensitive application settings;
it remains in the selected private project and its intended encrypted or
otherwise authorized handover. Generic product code contains none of those
customer values.

## Complete native purposes

| GovHub purpose | Action | Native operation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CAPTURE | castor-capture | Receive the complete selected project and native inventory |
| BACKUP_CREATE | castor-backup | Run the selected existing backup task, receive every declared output and verification |
| PREVIEW | castor-preview | Run the chosen existing task on the selected Candidate/Rehearsal environment |
| REHEARSAL | castor-restore | Run the selected restore against the original hash-bound recovery inputs |
| CUTOVER | castor-release | Apply the selected original release task under the existing reviewed plan |
| ROLLBACK | castor-rollback | Run the original recovery task and verify the selected recovery result |

Every mutation requires the reviewed original source commit, application task
and explicit verification task/checks. Backup requires declared complete
output paths. Restore and Rollback require original hash-bound input files.
A task is selected by its actual native name; tool maintenance, remote package
execution, repack and compile are not interchangeable defaults for an
application mutation. Applications may expose their own reviewed build or
release task, whose source and outputs are retained.

Before dispatch, the provider captures the full original source. Missing
declared *future output* files may be absent at this stage; their absence is
recorded, not filled with a placeholder. It then freshly compares source
content, index/worktree, submodule identities, executable identities,
selected configuration, native engine and recovery input bytes. A changed
source refuses dispatch under the old reviewed instruction.

The existing Session records the exact command before starting its process.
It records stdout/stderr, actual return code, original PID and invocation
time, and retains the exact original command receipt. Native process-group
cancellation and deadlines remain the existing Session implementation.

After an actual successful exit:

1. Run the selected verification task once through the same original command
   journal. Its unknown exit is also retained; verification is not blindly
   repeated after loss.
2. Receive the actual complete JSON stdout or declared file. The full report
   is frozen by hash before evaluating the selected JSON pointers.
3. Compare every actual observed value with the selected expected value.
   JSON types matter; false, zero and an empty string are distinct.
4. Inventory every declared complete output, including every ordinary file
   in each selected directory. A missing or changed original output prevents
   complete receiving.
5. Receive the actual following native inventory and full post-task source
   under a different source phase. New SQL/files/PHAR/image bytes are included
   without executing the task again.
6. Retain the exact original verification, task exit, before/after source and
   output/input identities in the completed native result.

A zero task exit alone does not mean backup or restoration was verified.
The selected task's report determines its actual application-specific
coverage. SQL and files are not labelled a transactional snapshot unless the
original native producer establishes that property.

## Process loss, native receipts and reopening

There is no added task queue or background provider worker. Castor executes
in the original native Session. If the application process may have started
but no complete original exit receipt exists, the operation remains
WAITING_NATIVE. The same command is never reissued merely because a browser,
parent process, transport or receiving host was lost.

The operator first reconciles that exact original process on its original
host. Preserve the original command directory and all output prefixes.
If its complete actual Session receipt exists elsewhere, select that
ordinary absolute receipt path in the continuation field
castor_command_receipt. This is the actual command JSON produced by the
original Session, together with its referenced full stdout/stderr files,
not an operator-written exit code.

The receiver requires the receipt's original argv, cwd, start time,
mutating/input binding and known PID to match the interrupted original. It
requires an observed complete exit and verifies both full output files by
size and hash. Every incoming receipt and prior interrupted record is
retained before the recovered native completion is adopted. A nonzero
observed exit remains the original failure.

Normal Resume uses the original operation ID, retained request digest and
checkpoint. Complete command records reopen without redispatch, including
when an explicitly selected receiving host has different executable paths.
An unresolved old process cannot become a new process on that host.

Completed source receiving and project reopening use the helper's exact
same-packet identity. The source-before and source-after archives remain
separate even when they have the same Git HEAD. That distinction preserves
a native backup task's new outputs and prevents a resumed source stage from
mistaking an earlier archive for its completed following edition.

## Provider and helper integration

The module exports the existing provider functions:

    provider_schema()
    profile(config, runtime_bindings=None)
    provider_context(profile)
    actions_for(operation_type)
    pollable(resume_checkpoint)
    resume_fields(operation, payload, reason)
    discover_capabilities(config, runtime_bindings=None)
    capture(config, context, checkpoint=None, cancelled=None)
    execute(operation, config, source_paths, checkpoint=None, cancelled=None)

The original application Session owns command admission, execution,
cancellation, stdout/stderr, events and native-state.json. The provider calls
the adjacent source helper as:

    capture_source(session, native_inventory, selected_profile)

The selection also carries capture_phase (capture, before or after) and
allow_missing_task_outputs only for the before phase. Original helper
verify_source, receive_source and reopen_source verify/receive the full
archive and reopen native Git/project source without a second application
engine. Consult CASTOR_SOURCE.md for exact complete helper inputs and
independent receiving.

Result statuses remain COMPLETE, WAITING_NATIVE, FAILED or CANCELLED.
native_resume identifies the original command, process observation and
request hash. pollable is false because a local command has no separate
provider-job polling API.

COMPLETE observations include original native_inventory/before_inventory,
source/before_source, task_result, verification, complete task_outputs and
backup_inputs, and original request_sha256. These are actual received
native results. No adoption, payment, client approval or visual acceptance
is implied by source completion.

## Whole installed acceptance

Use the existing full GovHub native course and browser course with the
selected actual application and original operator identity. It must cover:

- selected task/context/source and real native Docker image cohort;
- complete backup and actual declared SQL/files outputs;
- an explicitly selected nonproduction restoration and native verification;
- original process/transport interruption and same-operation continuation;
- full source/project archive download and independent receiving/reopen;
- actual operator screens and all outgoing source/report/downloads.

The producing operator must open the **exact outgoing version**, inspect
actual wide and narrow screenshots, use important controls, download the
complete outputs, and reopen the original project. Source syntax, DOM
counts and this guide are not rendered acceptance. Preserve the original
receiving operation while equipment is unavailable and continue substantive
source work; do not declare a queued operation complete.

## License and boundaries

Authored provider/guide code is Apache-2.0 under the existing GovHub license.
Selected upstream Castor originals retain their MIT license and exact source
identities. Public product source contains generic code and original public
contracts only. Selected customer source, configuration, image layers,
database/files, private task output and commercial correspondence belong
to the operator's original private project and authorized delivery.

Directory recovery inputs declare kind: directory and use the actual output manifest_sha256 as sha256; the manifest is the canonical ordered members array of relative path, bytes and SHA-256. File inputs default to kind: file. The full directory bytes are in the source archive; the directory identity is not a fabricated database backup file. Keep the original restore task arguments and real native directory path.

## Complete private state and bounded operating checkpoints

Every native state remains complete in its original private Session. The operating callback carries an immutable SHA-256/byte-bound `native_state` reference plus the actual phase, original request and pending-command fields, so a large Git inventory does not exceed the existing 1 MiB operation checkpoint boundary. The full state member is retained beside its original command records, included as an original native artifact in returned outcomes and preserved by whole-workspace backup. Receiving resolves only the existing workspace custody relocation and verifies every original byte before reopening the state. No task/source member is omitted or summarized to fit the operating checkpoint. Selected submodules must be initialized; a parent repository cannot stand in for a missing nested checkout.

# Receive the complete Castor operating project

This programme uses the installed GovHub application, its original private workspace, existing native Castor tasks and the selected Docker/Compose application. It preserves each original request, command receipt, verification report, declared output, complete source package and project backup. It does not install a task engine, create an account or schedule a deployment.

The source edition includes the provider, complete task and verification controls in the browser, the command-line receiving programme, full source/export helper, existing workspace backup and an independent application receiving path. Source review, actual native execution and rendered acceptance are separate outcomes.

## Inputs and original ownership

Select the existing GovHub workspace, complete original supplied-input directory, staff username and password environment reference. Keep its original application source and assessment engine together. Select one existing local environment record with its actual provider_resource_id equal to the profile's logical deployment identity. For a preview task its purpose must be Candidate or Rehearsal. A reviewed restore, release or rollback also requires its original comparison plan and revision.

Use the actual Castor executable or repacked application, selected native PHP launcher when applicable, complete Git checkout, Docker executable and original Docker context. The selected current source contract is Castor v1.8.1. A PHAR source installation requires the release's own PHP requirement; a static executable carries its own runtime. Do not assume the system PHP used by another product is suitable.

The profile retains exact task name and argument tokens, Castor context, ordered Compose files, Compose project, original release files and selected immutable images. These values are application-specific. No example task or service name is a customer default. Native list and help output identify the actual installed task. Keep private configuration, runtime captures and customer files on the authorized private host.

For every mutating task choose an existing verification task that emits its real JSON report on stdout or in a selected project-relative file. Declare JSON pointers and their actual expected values. A successful process exit alone does not establish a successful release, backup or restoration.

## Complete course request

Copy native/castor/receiving.example.json into the private receiving area and replace every SELECT placeholder with an actual input. The schema is govhub-castor-native-receiving/v1. Each step has a unique id, native action, existing local environment record, complete profile and original authorization. The example contains initial capture, backup, nonproduction operation, reviewed restore and following capture. Select only the authorized course; release/rollback use the same existing operation engine and explicit reviewed plan.

The work_directory belongs to this one immutable original request. The programme saves its whole original request hash and rejects another request in that directory. Do not edit a submitted request to work around a paused or interrupted native task.

Run through the installed public launcher or the same complete Python source:

~~~sh
govhub --python /ABS/ORIGINAL_PYTHON castor-receive run --request /PRIVATE/original-course.json
govhub --python /ABS/ORIGINAL_PYTHON castor-receive status --request /PRIVATE/original-course.json
~~~

Direct equivalent:

~~~sh
/ABS/ORIGINAL_PYTHON /ABS/GOVHUB/workspace/castor_receive.py run --request /PRIVATE/original-course.json
~~~

The whole saved sequence is leased serially. Each native step retains its original profile, configuration result, queue request, operation ID and complete returned operation. Repeating run continues the same original sequence. A completed step is received from its original operation; it is not issued again. Exit 2 means the retained course needs attention. Exit 0 means the command completed its stated action; inspect the complete returned state.

## Receive selected values from earlier steps

profile_sources can select a native scalar from a prior COMPLETE operation using an explicit JSON pointer. The example obtains source_revision from the actual initial capture's native_inventory.head_commit. The receiver stores that original operation ID, revision, hash, pointer and value.

A JSON field may use encoding: json to preserve a complete original value as JSON text. Runtime paths and credential environment names cannot be rebound by these source selectors. They remain explicit host selections.

For backup to restore, use backup_sources:

~~~json
{
  "backup_sources": [
    {"step":"02-backup","path":"ACTUAL_SQL_OUTPUT","target_path":"ACTUAL_RECEIVED_SQL_INPUT"},
    {"step":"02-backup","path":"ACTUAL_FILES_DIRECTORY","target_path":"ACTUAL_RECEIVED_FILES_DIRECTORY"}
  ]
}
~~~

Each selection must name exactly one complete declared output from the earlier original operation. A file contributes its complete SHA-256; a directory contributes the hash of its complete original member manifest. The receiver binds path, role, kind and original hash into backup_inputs_json and preserves the complete output record in its receiving journal. target_path is an explicitly selected project-relative destination; omitting it keeps the original relative path.

The native provider verifies that actual destination file or directory before executing the selected restore task. This selection does not copy files, rewrite native task arguments or invent a backup archive. Receive the original complete package into the authorized target and select the existing native restore task's real arguments. The helper transports directory bytes and modes separately in the complete source archive.

## Same-command recovery

Castor local processes use the original GovHub Session. They are not converted into a polling job service. An unknown mutation remains attached to its original command and process. No new command is launched merely because a previous control connection ended.

When the actual original process has completed, retain its complete Session command JSON and original stdout/stderr files. A continuation has schema govhub-castor-native-continuation/v1, the exact original request_sha256 and operations keyed by the original operation ID:

~~~json
{
  "schema":"govhub-castor-native-continuation/v1",
  "request_sha256":"ACTUAL_ORIGINAL_REQUEST_SHA256",
  "operations":{
    "ACTUAL_ORIGINAL_OPERATION_ID":{
      "castor_command_receipt":"/PRIVATE/ACTUAL_ORIGINAL_COMPLETED_COMMAND.json",
      "reason":"Receive this same original native process and its complete observed outputs"
    }
  }
}
~~~

Run the same request with --continuation /PRIVATE/original-continuation.json. The provider checks exact original argv, working directory, start identity, process ID when known, stdin/mutating selection, actual observed exit and full output sizes/hashes. Supplying a typed exit code is not a completion receipt. A nonzero original exit stays a failed native task.

runtime_bindings may supply only the provider's declared original host path fields: site_root, castor_path, php_path, git_path and docker_path. It cannot replace task, source, Docker context, Compose project or reviewed inputs. Include the existing paths of the receiving host; the complete private project retains its prior command and source history.

The receiver may resume a paused or waiting pre-dispatch step under its saved revision-bound request key. It does not resume an ambiguous mutation without its actual receipt. Cancellation remains explicit: resume_cancelled must be selected in the continuation before a cancelled operation is reconsidered. A failed task is not automatically replayed.

For a reviewed restore/release/rollback, the existing comparison engine may require the actual restored inventory. Supply its original restored_snapshot_id in the step or explicit continuation after that inventory has been retained. Native provider completion is recorded independently from the existing cohort comparison.

Build and verify the full source application with its selected source lock using build_application.py. Keep the resulting complete application ZIP and SHA-256. The receiving selection names:

- destination: a new absolute private directory separate from source inputs, original workspace and receiving journal;
- application_zip and application_sha256: the complete verified application;
- source_exports: original completed step, exact operation file name and optional existing host path bindings.

Each initial/following CAPTURE step must have a selected complete source archive. Additional before/after task source archives may be selected from their original completed steps.

The receiver reads each actual operation artifact and verifies its complete bytes/hash before opening the archive. It checks the original logical environment, Castor entrypoint/context, Docker context, Compose project and ordered files, release/output/backup selections, original capture phase, actual source commit and full original source-result target. The native source helper validates every complete archived member, receives it in a separate directory and reopens original Git and working source through the actual selected Git executable.

Image archives remain complete original recovery inputs. Independent source receiving does not load images, start containers, execute Castor tasks or import a database. An authorized native restore/release is a separately selected original operating step.

The same handover also copies complete original GovHub supplied inputs, verifies/unpacks the full application, creates a coherent private workspace backup, checks all completed course operations, then launches a separate Python process from the received application. The original course request/state travel with the backup.

Repeating handover uses its same retained selection, source archives and output directories. It validates already-received files instead of replacing them with another source. Retain complete private archives with their authorized recipient; they can contain account configuration and customer data.

## Actual browser receiving

native/castor/browser_receive.cjs uses the equipped host's already-installed Playwright and browser. It installs nothing and launches no provider task. Copy browser.example.json to the private operation and select actual origin, existing staff credential reference, local environment IDs, completed or attention-state operation IDs, exact download names and output directory.

~~~sh
node /ABS/GOVHUB/workspace/native/castor/browser_receive.cjs /PRIVATE/original-browser-course.json
~~~

The course opens the exact installed application, signs in through its native login, captures desktop and 390-pixel views, operates task and verification selection in the unsaved editor, opens original source definitions, visits the native task instruction, opens original operation and receiving-host controls, and downloads the selected complete artifacts through their actual UI links. Every download must match its original size and SHA-256. It exercises the real browser transport failure/recovery state and reopens the same operation in a separate browser session.

The result records actual screenshots, browser errors, selected views, download identities and original reopened operation. It marks visible overflow or browser errors as repair required. Otherwise its state remains RENDERED_AWAITING_VISUAL_INSPECTION. A person or the actual visual reader must open and inspect every screenshot, record concrete findings and rerun affected views after repair. Missing task/backup/source inputs are reported, not simulated. Retain actual empty/loading/failed/complete states from this course; do not claim a state was reviewed if it never occurred.

# Complete native Castor source receiving

This helper accompanies the existing GovHub Castor operation. The existing Castor adapter selects and runs the application's actual tasks through its original Session. Source capture reads that selected native project and produces one complete private archive for the selected capture phase.

## What is retained

Each capture includes the full original Git bundle, refs, HEAD archive, staged and unstaged binary patches, current index listing, exact tracked/untracked worktree bytes and recursively initialized submodules. The submodule's actual checkout HEAD remains distinct from the parent index gitlink, so a deliberately changed submodule checkout remains visible. Index conflicts and unavailable submodules need explicit operator attention.

Original Compose files, Castor entrypoint, release PHAR/binary/configuration files, recovery input files/directories and task output files/directories are retained exactly as selected. Directory identities use the same canonical complete list of file path, byte length and SHA256 as the native provider. Directory archives additionally retain directory modes and empty directories. Selected files may be Git-ignored; unrelated ignored caches and host secrets are not copied implicitly. The actual selected Castor executable is retained separately with its original bytes and mode, including when it lives outside the project.

Docker Compose's original image rows are retained unchanged. Their short IDs are resolved through the selected Docker engine's native image inspection to full immutable image IDs and repository digests. The helper saves those actual full IDs using native Docker image-save and retains the complete resulting tar bytes. An explicit image selection uses full IDs or repository digests; an empty selection uses the complete current image cohort reported by the selected Compose project. A Compose project without created containers may have no current images: that actual empty census remains explicit, and the helper does not pull or build images.

The original provider inventory, Docker engine identity, Compose configuration, native commands, complete stdout/stderr and command receipts remain archive members. The helper adds archive, manifest and each command file through the existing Session. The provider carries those same actual artifacts into its completed result and full GovHub handover.

The caller supplies the original profile and inventory:

The helper adds capture_phase equal to capture, before or after. Each phase receives its own immutable selection, command labels and source directory even when Git HEAD is unchanged. ## Complete package

The outer file is castor-source.zip. Its MANIFEST.json uses schema govhub-castor-source/v1 and contains the exact target, source_revision, complete members with bytes/SHA256/modes, repositories, selected source/output/input parts, image archive details and original command references.

The whole archive, including its manifest and ZIP framing, must fit the original max_artifact_bytes. Overflow retains the original partial capture in ATTENTION rather than marking it complete. Raising the selected intake bound is an explicit original profile/runtime decision; the helper does not omit large files.

The archive is private. It can include complete application data, explicit backup contents, Compose configuration and native command output. Keep it in the existing private GovHub workspace and original authorized project handover. Public application source contains no native archive data or credentials.

The files are acquired at their actual native observation times. Their application/database consistency is established only by the selected original backup task and its actual verification result. Capturing file hashes and Docker images does not assert a transactional database snapshot.

## API

capture_source(session, inventory, selection) returns state COMPLETE with target, source_revision, archive and manifest paths, exact archive_identity, complete files, repositories and parts. It uses Session.command, Session.add and the original checkpoint/state. It creates no second task executor, remote account or operation queue.

verify_source(archive_path, max_bytes=...) validates the complete member set and every byte/hash without extracting files or contacting Docker.

receive_source(archive_path, new_private_directory, max_bytes=...) copies all exact members into a private directory. The original archive SHA binds continuation; a different archive cannot reuse that receiving directory. The original complete package is retained independently of the source host.

reopen_source(session, received_directory, new_checkout_directory) reconstructs original Git refs, detached HEAD, staged changes, exact local files and initialized submodules. It fetches HEAD and detaches the fresh checkout before restoring original branch refs, preserving the initialized branch safety rule. It compares the native final index, status and binary patches with the original retained outputs. It also restores the explicitly selected release/configuration/input/output files and verifies their original hashes. Complete image-save bytes stay in the received package.

A receiving-only Session may use a validated Git executable, the original timeout/max-size values, an empty private host directory and existing relocation mappings. It does not need a fabricated Castor entrypoint or Compose files. Apply the full Castor provider profile only after the original checkout exists.

receive_command_receipt(session, actual_receipt_path) reconciles an interrupted command in that independent source Session. It requires the original argv, working directory, start time, PID, stdin and mutation flag, actual completed exit and complete original stdout/stderr hashes. Both the unchanged incoming receipt and original interrupted record are retained. The enclosing course supplies this through its original request-bound continuation; it does not change the frozen archive or checkout selection. After receipt, call reopen_source again on that same Session. An unknown Git exit is never inferred or replaced by a new task.

Receiving does not load images, start containers, overwrite a live database or invoke a deployment/restore/verification task. Those are separately selected native actions owned by the existing operation. The result explicitly records image_load_performed=false and native_task_performed=false. Later legitimate edits to a completed independent checkout remain the receiving engineer's edits.

## Native continuation and verification

Original command admission and uncertain exit recovery remain Session's responsibility. An interrupted native command resumes by its original record/receipt; it is not relabeled as another task. Private source copies and selection declarations preserve their original hashes. Each incomplete capture rechecks current Git/index/worktree, selected original outputs, Compose configuration/cohort and Docker engine against its retained inventory before it can finish.

Keep the full application, actual Castor/Docker/Git runtime identities, selected profile and original source archive together. Use the complete Castor receiving course for actual source capture, original task/verification result, backup, separate application/workspace reopen and rendered product inspection. Source parsing alone does not establish a completed native commissioning.

## Cohort plans, exact findings and reviewer decisions

`plans.create` accepts `{name,baseline_id,candidate_id,agency_ids,min_agencies?,owner?,window_start?,window_end?,rollback_reference?,notes?}`. `agency_ids` must be explicit, unique native comparison IDs. `min_agencies` defaults to their count. `plans.revise` takes the same fields plus `{plan_id,expected_revision,reason}`; a revision preserves every older plan and decision. Dates are actual offset-bearing instants. `plans.get {plan_id,revision?}` returns `{plan,versions,baseline,candidate,approvals,audits,reviews,operations}`. `plan` contains the creation fields and summary fields above.

`audits.run {plan_id,expected_revision}` invokes unchanged `cutover.audit` on the pinned selected source rows and applicable exact field approvals. It returns `{audit}` with `{id,plan_id,plan_revision,sha256,created_at,author,status,summary,scope_issues,inputs,report}`. `summary` is the unchanged native summary with its per-site checks; `report` is the original tool report, not a rewritten score. `scope_issues` separately identifies any declared comparison IDs missing from both sources. The combined status is `PASS` only when the original audit and declared scope both pass. HTTP failure and missing sites stay visible as actual defects.

`approvals.save {plan_id,expected_revision,agency_id,field,before,after,reason}` requires a reviewer and exact currently pinned differing values. `field` is one of `canonical_url`, `export_sha256`, `backup_sha256`, `route_count`. `before` and `after` are the exact native string values shown by the findings. New plan revisions can reuse an earlier exact field decision only when the same plan's source values and comparison ID still match; every reused decision retains its original plan revision and author.

`reviews.save {plan_id,expected_revision,audit_id,decision,reason}` requires a reviewer; `decision` is `APPROVE` or `RETURN`. Approval applies only to the exact current successful audit and full plan revision. The returned immutable review is `{id,plan_id,plan_revision,audit_id,decision,reason,author,created_at}`. ## Native operation lifecycle

`operations.create` accepts `{plan_id,expected_revision,type,environment_id,authorization_reference,request_key,agency_ids?,backup_sha256?,target_fingerprint?,native_action?}`. Types are `REHEARSAL`, `CUTOVER`, and `ROLLBACK`. Rehearsal and rollback select the plan's baseline; cutover selects its candidate. A cutover requires the current pinned audit and reviewer approval. `agency_ids` is the explicitly selected nonempty subset of the plan for this native environment; it defaults to the whole cohort. A backup selector identifies one exact retained backup. `target_fingerprint` is the actual Drush target fingerprint returned by capabilities and is checked again by the native adapter. `native_action` is pinned as `drush-restore` or `acquia-restore` and must match the profile. A `sources.capture` operation has type `CAPTURE` and action `drush-capture` or `acquia-capture`; it completes with source artifacts separately from restoration. Environment configuration explicitly identifies the real target and its operating authority.

`operations.get {operation_id}` returns `{operation,events,files}`. The operation preserves the complete selected plan, source snapshot, target record revision, authorization reference and native adapter configuration fingerprint. `progress` is `{completed,total,stage,detail}`. States are `QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, `PAUSED`, `WAITING_NATIVE`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, and `COMPLETE`.

`operations.cancel {operation_id,expected_revision,reason}` records cancellation and cooperatively interrupts owned work. `operations.resume {operation_id,expected_revision,reason,request_key}` resumes retained safe checkpoints. The worker rehashes retained source files before use. A lost or interrupted mutating native call enters `WAITING_NATIVE`; a second restore or cutover is not silently submitted. Its original target/result must be reconciled first.

An accepted Acquia restore keeps its exact original notification URL and automatically continues notification reads at a persisted five-second interval. Restart resumes that notification; it does not submit another restore request. Cancellation stops owned polling while preserving the actual already-submitted provider action and its continuation identity.

`operations.observe {operation_id,expected_revision,capture_file_id,restored_snapshot_id,actual_started_at,actual_finished_at,notes}` attaches an actual provider/native execution capture and a new original-format observed result snapshot. The backend checks source/target/operation identity and runs the unchanged original comparator between the operation's selected source and observed result. It retains the capture and resulting audit. Completion follows the actual successful capture plus the exact source comparison. A failed result remains an actionable operation with full per-site findings and its original artifacts.

`operations.configure {environment_id,expected_revision,config}` is admin-only; `expected_revision` is the displayed environment entity revision. It retains an immutable native profile and revisions that environment's `native_profile` field. Return is `{environment,profile:{revision,config}}`. Profile values use the adapter's current `configuration_schema()` types, including numeric backup ID/timeouts/artifact limits and actual Drush project/public-files paths. Secrets are environment-variable names or native existing session references. `operations.capabilities {environment_id}` returns `{environment,profile,current_config,configured,capabilities,configuration_schema}`. The native adapter source and original provider contracts are documented in `NATIVE_SOURCES.md`. Operation summaries include the actual native action and explicit comparison-ID subset. Plan `execution` reports verified cutover/rollback IDs and remaining IDs using each current revision's latest actual completed operations.

`operations.compare {before_id,after_id}` compares retained operation source/result snapshots and timing with exact revisions. A rollback is its own operation linked to the original plan and baseline; it does not overwrite a cutover's result.

All native data remains in the selected operator environment. Provider writes and DNS changes are represented only by actual configured operations or retained original execution captures. Customer-specific site inventory, account access, hosting configuration, acceptance authority, and recovery objectives are supplied by the operating prime.

`workspace.backup {destination}` requires an admin and creates the original full private-backup format at a new absolute directory. It copies the SQLite snapshot, reconciliation key, every registered source/output blob, and the complete `native-operations/` tree: original command/state/event records, stdout/stderr, native source/staging files and displaced public-file custody. Copies stream in fixed chunks, retain exact original journal bytes and record native relative paths/hashes in `backup.json.native_storage`. The private backup includes staff credentials.

A shared native-storage lease spans each worker claim and execution. Backup takes its exclusive side; actual active or unreconciled running work returns `409 BACKUP_NATIVE_ACTIVE` before creating the destination. The idle worker resumes claiming work after the copy releases its lease. Source or copy failure retains `BACKUP_INCOMPLETE`, which the original core refuses to open. Completed copies reopen at a new directory. `workspace_relocations:[{from,to}]` supplies the original private workspace roots to the native adapter; it resolves only private source/operation paths in memory when consuming existing records. Original command and source capture bytes, native target paths, profile identities, environment IDs, intent hashes and operation IDs remain unchanged. Accepted remote operations continue from their original notification after relocation.

A cohort handover also includes the original CAPTURE operations referenced by its selected snapshot bindings, with their original events, result envelopes and artifacts, as well as that plan's restores and observations. Unrelated capture operations are excluded by their retained file and comparison-ID relationships.

## Capture and bind the full source

Choose **Capture original source**. The native query retains the project, its current authorized environment array, services, volumes, routes, API-route bindings, backups, tasks and Lagoon version. It omits native array limits and retains all returned members.

The pinned backup resolver ignores its `includeDeleted` argument. The captured backup population therefore retains every returned backup and its original `deleted` value; it is not relabeled as a provider-filtered live-only population. The inventory also omits credentials, private keys, environment-variable values and task command/log bodies.

The completed capture includes `lagoon-source-inventory.json` and its original CLI source. Use the retained source files to build the actual six-column cohort inventories and per-site bindings. Existing site comparison IDs, owning-agency IDs and native environment IDs remain separate identities.

## Download the original backup

Select the opaque native `backupId` in the profile, then choose **Download selected native backup**. This purpose does not require a cohort plan.

Lagoon's `addRestore` prepares the original backup for downloading. The resulting archive is retained as a source artifact; application restoration is a separate native operation. GovHub first observes the original backup's existing restore row and reuses it when present. Otherwise it submits one original preparation command and retains its native restore ID.

Accepted work is observed by that same restore ID. `SUCCESSFUL` permits retrieval of the native download link. The provider's `restoreSize` is a byte count. The completed archive must be nonempty and match that declared count when one is available. The manifest retains its backup and restore identities, SHA-256, byte count and original locator source.

The backup resolver can remove an expired restore row after a failed object-store check. An absent later row does not authorize another preparation request. The original mutation, retained ID and any response gap remain available for operating continuation.

A completed archive response is recovered before requesting another native locator. If the process ended after the download but before the manifest or final checkpoint, GovHub verifies the retained original response record and exact bytes and finishes that same operation. Expired signed links do not invalidate an already retained complete archive.

Signed download locations and full native responses remain in the private operation material. The ordinary progress display retains the destination without its query string. Each incomplete or failed download attempt keeps its own original request and response path.

## Switch, observe and roll back

Choose a reviewed cohort and an environment which is the project's actual current standby. **Cutover** uses the approved candidate; **Rollback** uses the original baseline; **Rehearsal** uses the designated rehearsal target. A native command applies to the complete selected site cohort on that environment.

The adapter reads the complete project immediately before dispatch. It resolves the active and standby by their actual native names, normalized selectors and integer IDs, checks matching service names, and verifies that the reviewed target and API-route assignments remain the same. Native `makeSafe` lowercases the environment name and replaces each non-ASCII letter/digit/hyphen UTF-16 unit with a hyphen; its separate namespace truncation helper is not used for switch selection.

A switch retains the original native task ID on the reviewed standby environment. The provider can insert that task before a queue or response failure. If its response is lost, use **Operating continuation → Original Lagoon task ID**, with the actual task and operating reason. GovHub checks the task's identity, name, environment and pre-operation task population before following it. An ID returned by the original switch response is retained immediately. A manually supplied ID becomes authoritative only after native identity verification; an unverified or mistyped candidate remains correctable, with its prior attempts retained. It never creates a replacement switch to rediscover an earlier result.

A successful task is followed by a complete project readback. Completion requires:

- The active and standby roles resolve to the expected original environment IDs.
- The complete production and standby URL memberships match their separately reviewed sets.
- The original API-route IDs retain their domain, service, source and type, with attached ACTIVE/STANDBY routes on their expected new environments.
- Unattached and STANDARD routes retain their original assignments; missing, changed or additional routes remain visible as exact findings.

Lagoon rebuilds its route strings from migrated ingress rules. GovHub retains those raw values and compares URL membership, so native order changes or previously stale strings do not produce a false mismatch.

### Keep the native rollback selectors usable

The pinned provider's completion handler can write an environment's original name into the project's selector fields, while its next switch resolver expects `makeSafe(name)`. This matters for names containing slashes or other replaced characters.

When needed, the operation records a native `updateProject` step that writes only the two equivalent production/standby selectors for the same original environment IDs. It retains the exact preimage, project ID, originating switch task, command and readback. This step may require the native account's `project:update` permission in addition to the switch permissions. It does not move routes, deploy an application or rewrite environment variables.

The same correction is available before a switch when the existing selectors came from an earlier native completion. An unknown correction response is reconciled against the current native values; the original command identity remains retained. A later continuation can finish an already applied correction without another switch or project write.

After the native task and readback complete, the cohort operation remains at **Attach the actual restored observation**. Select the completed original execution capture and the actual RESTORED inventory for the same source cohort. The existing auditor compares that observed inventory against the pinned source and records the final result.

# Native Drupal and Acquia operations

`native_adapter.py` connects the maintained GovHub operator to an existing Drupal host or the selected Acquia Cloud environment. The original author’s `../cutover.py` remains the comparison engine. Its original Git blob is `5800656de67569524560c84bdd437634f0c7f22a`, source merge `abc45bf4fd25402ef7a846819abc235bdeebfa5d`, SHA-256 `677dabb175d47ce4655a3ea0f511bde7b58ee51ecff0a4a4333377ffca5ff3a2`.

The backend owns named staff, environment records, source custody, reviewed plans, immutable source pins and operation leases. This adapter owns the real native commands, API requests, retained bytes and resumable native outcomes. A completed native restoration returns its actual target and source identity; the backend then takes an actual restored manifest through the unchanged comparison.

## Configuration and interface

The web interface uses `configuration_schema()` to render ordinary labeled fields. It returns `version`, `selector: "source_kind"`, and `providers[]` with `value`, `label`, and `fields[]`. Each field exposes `name`, `label`, `type`, `required`, and applicable `help`, `placeholder`, `default`, `minimum`, or `maximum` values. `discover_capabilities(config)` returns this schema, `current_config`, `configuration`, observed `native_status`, `provider_context`, `target_fingerprint`, `actions`, `ready`, `observed_at`, and any concrete readiness message.

| Provider | Required configuration | Restoration-specific configuration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `drush` | `environment_id`, existing `drush_path`, absolute existing `site_root`, `uri`; optional `php_path` and existing local `site_alias` | `restore_destination`, the existing project root containing `site_root`; `files_relative_path`, the actual public files path relative to that project |
| `acquia` | `environment_id`, `database_name`, `access_token_env` | `backup_id`, the actual completed backup selected from that same environment and database |

`environment_id` inside the profile is the native provider reference. The carrier’s own environment entity has a separate local ID. It supplies `operation.provider_environment_id` explicitly; the adapter compares that value with the profile. `operation.environment_id` remains the local entity ID in the carrier’s records.

`timeout_seconds` accepts 10–7,200 seconds. `max_artifact_bytes` bounds a single retained artifact and the expanded public-files restoration set; its default is 1 GiB. The adapter reads Acquia’s existing access token from the environment variable named by `access_token_env`. Configuration and command records contain that variable name, not its value. The Acquia API origin is the published `https://cloud.acquia.com/api`.

The Drupal root and project root are different inputs. For an existing project at `/srv/pilot`, Drupal may run from `/srv/pilot/web`, with its files under `web/sites/default/files`. The actual `core:status` files path must agree with the reviewed profile. The adapter rejects remote Drush aliases because their filesystem is not the local artifact custody directory. Run the same adapter on the authorized native host that owns those paths.

```python
configuration_schema() -> dict
discover_capabilities(config: dict) -> dict
capture(config: dict, context: dict, checkpoint=None, cancelled=None) -> dict
execute(operation: dict, config: dict, source_paths: dict,
        checkpoint=None, cancelled=None) -> dict
```

`capture` receives `context.output_dir`, a new or continued private capture directory. The result contains `status`, `artifacts`, `provider_context`, `observations`, `events`, and `checkpoint`/`resume_checkpoint`.

`execute` receives the carrier’s exact selected sources:

```json
{
  "snapshot_id": "the-original-snapshot-id",
  "snapshot_sha256": "the-reviewed-snapshot-sha256",
  "rows": [],
  "bindings": [{
    "agency_id": "the-source-agency-id",
    "export": {"path": "/private/export.json", "sha256": "…", "size": 0},
    "backup": {
      "path": "/private/backup.tar.gz", "sha256": "…", "size": 0,

    },
```
