```json
  }],

```

The strings and sizes above describe the envelope; actual operations use the retained source values. Every artifact descriptor has `role`, `path`, `sha256`, and `size`. Preserve additional native metadata when the carrier copies it. A Drupal binding’s `files` contains the exact `database_dump` and every `configuration_file`, retaining each configuration file’s `relative_path`. Its `export` is the `drush-configuration-files/v1` manifest. Its `backup` is the original Drush archive. The adapter verifies all of these bytes and the complete configuration file set before restoration starts.

The operation names its `native_action`, `provider_environment_id`, reviewed `target_fingerprint`, and, when several sources exist, exact `agency_id` and/or `backup_sha256`. These native action names are independent of the carrier’s REHEARSAL, CUTOVER and ROLLBACK plan labels.

| Native action | Actual operation |
| --- | --- |
| `drush-capture` | Read native status and installed commands; export configuration; write the real SQL dump and native archive to private custody |
| `drush-restore` | Import the selected SQL, restore its retained public file members into the reviewed native files directory, import the complete selected configuration, rebuild caches, and retain new native status |
| `acquia-capture` | Read the selected environment and complete domain/backup inventories; optionally download the selected backup’s actual bytes |

## Drupal capture and restoration

The adapter observes installed commands with `list --format=json` and uses an explicit non-secret field list with `core:status --format=json`. Target fingerprints include the selected root, URI, database identity, files path, Drupal/Drush versions and relevant installed restoration commands. A new target requires a new reviewed fingerprint.

Capture runs the installed `config:export --destination=… --yes`, `sql:dump --result-file=…` and `archive:dump --destination=… --yes`. It preserves individual configuration files and their exact complete manifest, the separate SQL dump, the archive, and the native status. These artifacts describe the actual source site. Agency membership, route count, HTTP status, canonical URLs and approval decisions remain separate actual manifest observations.

The component restoration path uses the documented `sql:drop --yes` followed by an import appropriate to the observed database driver. MySQL/PostgreSQL use the configured Drush `sql:query --file=…` path without expanding a credential-bearing shell command. SQLite uses the installed Drupal `Settings::initialize()` and `Database::getConnection()` APIs, then passes the unchanged, hash-checked SQL to that driver's native PDO client. Drupal registers its own SQLite functions and `NOCASE_UTF8` collation when opening the connection; standalone `sqlite3` does not have that collation. The adapter's actual-driver preflight checks the resolved database file, selected dump and registered collation before reset. Its emitted PHP helper and request are retained with their hashes inside the operation, and the import returns the original driver source hash, database identity, source hash and native integrity-check result.

The installed Drush 13.8.0 SQLite driver constructs its dump with native `sqlite3 .dump`; that dump creates tables and does not replace tables already present. The explicit reset removes the selected target's tables, including stale tables absent from the recovery point. The adapter verifies and stages the exact SQL, configuration set and archive `files/` members before this first mutation. Reset and import are separate persisted mutating commands, so known completed steps remain reusable during the same operation's continuation. A retained, completed generic SQLite import with a nonzero exit code is preserved under its original label; the driver correction records a separate reset and import, clearing its partially applied schema. An unknown original completion must be reconciled before that correction. The pre-reset native status/command observation also remains available when a partial database can no longer complete Drupal bootstrap; current root, site, database and installed-version identities still have to agree. The adapter then restores the managed public files, imports configuration and rebuilds caches. The published reset contract is `https://www.drush.org/13.x/commands/sql_drop/`.

This action restores database, configuration and the original managed public-files tree into an already configured Drupal application. The installed application code, Composer dependencies and native database connection belong to that configured environment. The archive's original `MANIFEST.yml` is read through installed `yaml:get:value`: format `1.0`, an enabled files component and a Drush 13 generator are required for complete file reconciliation. Drush 13 explicitly excludes the public `css`, `js`, `styles` and `php` cache roots; those same roots remain outside the managed file comparison.

Before database reset, the adapter pins the full source public-file manifest and current target file inventory. Changed files and target-only files are copied into private `prior-public-files/` custody and hash-checked before replacement or removal. Each action records a prepared state before changing its target, then retains the actual completion; continuation recognizes an already-visible exact replacement/removal and checks original custody. The restored managed tree must match the complete selected source path, SHA-256, size and mode list. The operation returns the measured inventory artifact and hash, removal count, and explicit native cache exclusions. Original backup and displaced-file bytes remain part of the private operation handover.

The published Drush 13 command set provides this SQL/configuration path. An older `archive:restore` command must not be presumed present merely because an earlier manual describes it. Source-native command discovery determines what the configured host can run.

Archive extraction accepts ordinary files under `files/`, rejects link and special-file members, checks paths and expanded sizes, and stages bytes inside the private operation before changing native files. Every destination is checked against the selected project/files directory. The adapter does not execute an arbitrary shell string from a profile or manifest.

The selected environment ID is Acquia’s compound numeric-ID/application-UUID value. The adapter reads only that configured environment and database, using these original paths:

| --- | --- |
| GET | `/environments/{environmentId}` |
| GET | `/environments/{environmentId}/domains` |

The restore POST has no request body and restores the selected backup to its own environment/database. A 202 response supplies `_links.notification.href`. The adapter persists that exact notification and selected backup/source identity before returning a pending native state. Notification statuses are `in-progress`, `completed`, and `failed`. ## Checkpoints and interrupted operations

`checkpoint(value)` is called for each actual command/request and persisted native state. It receives:

```json
{
  "stage": "the-current-native-stage",
  "mutation_started": true,
  "safe_to_retry": true,
  "resume_checkpoint": {
    "intent_sha256": "…",
    "intent": {},
    "phase": "accepted",
    "environment_id": "the-native-environment-id",
    "database_name": "the-native-database-name",
    "backup_id": 123,
    "notification_url": "https://cloud.acquia.com/api/notifications/the-original-uuid"
  }
}
```

The carrier persists the callback before returning. It passes the retained `resume_checkpoint` directly as `source_paths.checkpoint` or `operation.resume_checkpoint` on the same operation. The local `native-state.json`, command records and original stdout/stderr remain in the private native output directory. Source hashes, target, action and original snapshot identity are checked together before continuation.

A complete workspace backup retains `native-operations/` and `sources/` bytes with the carrier's original-root inventory. When that backup opens elsewhere, the carrier supplies `workspace_relocations: [{"from": "/original/private/workspace", "to": "/current/private/workspace"}]` in both capture context and operation source paths. The adapter resolves only those two private directory prefixes in memory, including command arguments and artifact descriptors. Native environment/profile targets, settings, database paths, public-file targets and URLs remain unchanged. Original JSON requiring private-path resolution is also retained byte for byte under `relocated-originals/` before a continued mutable state record is saved. Completed command comparisons use their resolved private paths and the original output hashes; prior command/result/event bytes are not rewritten to manufacture new provenance.

`safe_to_retry` describes resuming this exact operation. For accepted Acquia work, continuation performs GET on the retained notification. It does not issue another POST. A response that reached local custody before a callback failure is reconciled from the original retained request and response bytes. A dispatched request without an accepted native identity remains associated with its original request for provider reconciliation.

For Drupal, each completed mutating command has an immutable request/result record, including its return code and stdout/stderr hashes. Continuation reuses completed commands. File restoration replaces exact selected bytes atomically and records each completed path; its prior bytes remain available. An interrupted child is stopped through its own process group. A native command whose completion is unknown remains attached to that original process/result; it is not silently started again. A launch failure before any child exists is recorded separately and can be resumed.

Results distinguish `COMPLETE`, `FAILED`, `WAITING_NATIVE` and `CANCELLED`. A cancellation after mutation began retains its native continuation for reconciliation. Native restore completion includes the original target, backup checksum and snapshot identity. The carrier uses an actual RESTORED source manifest to complete the broader cutover/recovery comparison.

GovHub can operate an existing Pantheon site through the host's installed Terminus CLI. Receive the complete GovHub application, including `pantheon_adapter.py`, `pantheon_receive.py` and all six files in `pantheon_bridge/`. ## 2. Capture inventory and retain exact backups

Choose **Capture original source**. The completed operation retains the actual site and environment metadata, selected environment's complete finished backup lists, native code logs and original Terminus command/output files. The source manifest distinguishes code, database and files backups.

Terminus returns backup size as rounded MB display text. Each downloaded archive gets its own exact byte count and SHA-256 from the retained bytes. Its native site, environment, filename and component identity stay attached.

There are two separate backup purposes:

- **Download selected native backup** fetches each filename already selected in the native profile. At least one component must be selected. Each command uses the exact filename and writes its bytes directly into the operation's private directory.
- **Create and retain a native backup** creates a complete environment backup, identifies its new code/database/files members, and downloads those exact original archives. It retains the before and after native backup populations and the original creation command.

## 3. Review a staging, release or rollback operation

Prepare the original six-column source inventories and cohort plan in GovHub. Choose the comparison IDs belonging to this native target. The operation retains the selected source snapshot, cohort revision, target environment, native profile revision and operating authorization.

The existing purposes remain:

| Purpose | Original source |
| --- | --- |
| Rehearsal | Baseline, using a designated rehearsal environment |
| Cutover | Candidate with its completed audit and approval for that exact revision |

For a Pantheon target, **Native action** is a selector with the following complete actions:

### Promote reviewed code

Select **Promote reviewed code to Test or Live**. A Test operation promotes Dev code. A Live operation promotes Test code. Copy the observed promotion source code-log SHA-256 into the native profile before preparing the operation.

The adapter compares the current source with that reviewed value before preparing the target backup and immediately before dispatch. It retains the actual target code log after the native deployment. ### Sync content, database or files

Select the exact source environment in the native profile. **Sync reviewed database and files** operates files and database as two separately recorded native commands. The database-only and files-only actions operate their named component.

The source and destination are explicit, distinct environments on the same site. Each must be initialized. The adapter uses Terminus's original `env:clone-content` semantics, including native WordPress search/replace behavior and the optional paired replacement text.

### Restore exact backup components

Select the original native backup filenames in the profile and bind their downloaded bytes into the cohort source snapshot. Restore validates the native site, environment, component and filename of every selected bound archive and verifies its retained bytes.

## 4. Continue the original provider work

Every native command has a durable argv, working directory, stdout, stderr and exit record under the original operation. New target-changing steps call the received `govhub:bridge` command through that same Session. Inventory and original archive reads continue to use the released native commands.

### Immediate native workflow retention

Before a new native mutation, the provider verifies the installed bridge against the three PHP source files in this exact application. It writes a private request with mode0600 that binds the original operation, step, immutable intent, site UUID, native environment and selected action. That request and its byte hash stay in the original operation directory.

The bridge persists the original dispatch before sending the native workflow request. It retains the complete native HTTP response and returned workflow UUID in its original receipt directory before returning process output. The provider consumes that same final receipt, immediate workflow sidecar or complete settled command result after an interrupted receiving write. Every retained native event and its bytes remain available with the operation.

An accepted workflow is followed by a separate read-only `workflow-inspect` request for the same UUID. The provider checks its original site, environment and workflow type. A running workflow keeps the existing operation pollable; a succeeded workflow finishes its original step; a failed workflow retains its actual failed result. A completed no-change code deployment retains the native observation without manufacturing a workflow.

If the command response is lost after native dispatch, the bridge's existing local recovery runs before login or another provider request. The provider retains the original command record and uses a distinct read command to obtain that same receipt. A dispatched step with no received native UUID stays attached to its original request and sidecars for the original workflow association.

A native validation failure before journal creation retains its completed stdout, command and request association. After correcting the receiving source or local request conditions, the same operation's manual continuation can create a distinct attempt. The original return remains in its command history. Receipt acquisition and actual dispatch recovery continue through their retained journal or workflow.

### Original operating continuation

Open **Operating continuation** when a provider command requires its original outcome. Select **Original provider workflow UUID** for the displayed pending command and retain the operating reason. GovHub checks that:

- The UUID is the actual native workflow selected by the operator.
- It was absent from the retained pre-command workflow population.
- Its current native status identifies the same site, target environment and expected native step type.
- It does not replace a workflow already verified and bound to that step.

The first valid native observation retains the association. A wrong-target candidate can be corrected on the same operation. Operations created before the bridge integration preserve their original native command, argv hash, prior workflow list and explicit UUID continuation; receiving the new source does not replace that history.

A complete rejected bridge receipt that confirms no native dispatch can be resumed after its actual configuration or input correction. That explicit continuation retains the previous rejected request and receipt and creates a separate next attempt for the same original step. A dispatched write remains associated with its original outcome.

A failed or interrupted archive read keeps its original command, output and partial file. A later continuation retries that same selected backup in a separate retained download attempt. A failed read-only bridge or inventory command can likewise be observed again after the native installation or account context is corrected. Completed successful observations keep their original output.

A native command can finish before the local receiving write. Recovery reads the retained completion, verifies its original artifacts, and finishes the same operation. It also recovers a completed final manifest before issuing fresh provider reads.

### Receive an original operation on another machine

First run `pantheon_receive.py prepare` with the receiving host's actual PHP, Terminus and CLI working directory. In the existing continuation form, enable **Use this receiving machine** and enter its prepared paths. The underlying `operations.resume` payload accepts:

The example paths and identifiers are explanatory values. The receiver's `call operations.resume --bind-runtime` fills the binding from its successful preparation and preserves both original and applied request payloads. `operations.capabilities` accepts the same binding for a receiving-host observation.

Only `terminus_path`, `php_path` and `site_root` belong in a runtime binding. An empty PHP value chooses a directly executable Terminus installation. The provider validates those actual local paths before Session begins, then records the receiving selection in the original native checkpoint. Site UUID, environment, source selection, restore filenames, code expectations, action and options remain pinned in the original business intent.

Historical raw argv and outputs remain intact. A completed original command is reused through its original record. A confirmed unstarted command or a failed settled read may select a distinct receiving-host command attempt with unchanged native arguments. An unresolved write continues through its original receipt or workflow. The original request/receipt private paths use the workspace's existing relocation map.

### Concurrent backup completion

A completed backup whose catalog is still appearing is followed through the original catalog observation without repeating creation. If more than one new backup per component appears while a backup command runs, the operation retains all candidates. **Operating continuation** then shows the original code, database and files filename choices. Select the exact three-member set belonging to that backup and resume. The selection is retained with the operating reason; the completed backup workflow is reused.

The workflow association, receiving runtime and backup selection fields all belong to the same original operation. Its reviewed source snapshot and pinned native profile remain available throughout continuation.

## 1. Prepare the existing native host

Set these path variables to the receiving operator's actual absolute paths. The examples below use variable references so the same commands work in a cloud receiving directory or an installed private service.

~~~bash
python3 "$GOVHUB_CODE/pantheon_receive.py" \
  --runtime-dir "$GOVHUB_RUNTIME" \
  prepare --php php --site-root "$GOVHUB_NATIVE_CWD"
~~~

To use an already received original release, add `--terminus-phar /absolute/path/terminus.phar`. To use a nondefault existing interpreter, set `--php /absolute/path/php`. Native executable symlinks are resolved to the actual interpreter. The receiver records the executable's full byte identity.

`prepare` performs the following native operation as one installation:

1. Inspect actual PHP version and extensions.
2. Verify the complete original release bytes and create the native launcher for this exact received source; run native `--version` through it.
3. Run PHP lint on the received bridge's PHP sources.
4. Call the unauthenticated `govhub:bridge-info` command.
5. If the matching bridge is absent from this installation, invoke native `self:plugin:install` with its retained bridge source directory and read the installed bridge again.
6. Compare every installed PHP source path, length and SHA-256 with the received source; load native bridge help.

A successful result returns `state: READY`, the exact private `runtime.json` artifact, installed version, installation ID and three native profile path values. `profile_runtime.terminus_path` selects the generated `terminus.php` launcher; pair it with `profile_runtime.php_path`. The unchanged release PHAR has its own `terminus` identity in the runtime record. Setup command records retain their original argv, working directory, complete stdout/stderr and process result. The runtime also records the three native directory bindings.

The runtime record is host-specific. Run `prepare` on a receiving host to inspect its installed tools and preserve its own runtime record. The received business target stays the original site UUID and environment.

### Updated source and moved applications

The native Terminus installer treats an existing package name as already installed. Repeating installation against a new application path therefore does not replace an older source binding. The receiver handles that case by selecting a native installation identified by the PHP/release identity and complete bridge runtime source. It retains ordinary copies of the bridge PHP files, Composer manifest and license inside that installation, then creates an immutable launcher there.

The launcher sets the native `TERMINUS_PLUGINS_DIR`, `TERMINUS_DEPENDENCIES_BASE_DIR` and `TERMINUS_COMMAND_CACHE_DIR` for the selected installation before starting the original PHAR with the exact PHP executable supplied to `prepare`. That executable can be the host's existing wrapper for PHP extension and configuration options. The launcher verifies both its bytes and the PHAR before dispatch, and invokes the selected executable again so the child retains those options. Native account/session locations come from the host's existing configuration. Identical source and launcher version reuse the same installation; changed source or launcher version receives a new installation. Moving an identical application can reuse the retained source even when the earlier application directory has gone away.

Launcher version 2 preserves the selected PHP entry point instead of restarting the raw `PHP_BINARY` path without its command options. Run `prepare` once to receive this launcher for an older installation. Its version is part of the immutable installation identity, so preparing the corrected launcher leaves the previous installation and its native command history intact. Preparation does not replay any saved provider operation.

Every later receiving command checks the launcher and retained plugin files against the received application. Native provider work reaches the same launcher through the existing three-path profile or `operations.resume --bind-runtime`. Its original arguments, working directory, standard streams and exit result pass through to Terminus; it remains in the original Session process group for timeout recovery. The native bridge still returns the original workflow receipt and UUID.

Use the returned `profile_runtime` values when configuring or resuming an operation. The receiver's `discover` command already selects this installation. For a direct read, invoke the prepared PHP and `terminus.php` paths together, for example `"$GOVHUB_PHP" "$GOVHUB_TERMINUS" govhub:bridge-info`.

### Bridge information ABI

The installed command returns `schema: govhub-pantheon-bridge-info/v1`, `terminus_version: 4.3.3`, `request_schema: govhub-pantheon-bridge/v1`, and `source_files`, a complete array of `{path, bytes, sha256}` for every received PHP file. Paths are relative to the plugin directory. The receiver compares the whole PHP source population and each original byte identity. The plugin also returns its version, root, supported actions and native source guard information.

The native bridge's private mutation receipts, dispatch/workflow sidecars and original workflow recovery are defined in `pantheon_bridge/PHP_BRIDGE.md`. Provider operations invoke that bridge through the maintained Pantheon adapter.

It retains the actual snapshot and returns the original workspace identity, actor, counts, worker state, and operation summaries. The source's bundled assessment core is the default; use `--assessment-core` only when that same unchanged source has been installed separately.

An original received backup is already an editable workspace. Select its absolute directory as `--workspace` and a separate existing intake directory as `--source-root`. The backup's `sources` directory is its private immutable blob store; the application opens those retained files through the original file records and backup metadata. It must not be used as the intake root. The intake and private workspace must be separate directories, with neither containing the other.

For a new explicitly selected workspace, initialize it through the existing `cli.py init` command described in `README.md`. The receiving command opens the original workspace supplied to it.

## 4. Configure the actual target through the original form or API

The **Environments** register retains the application's environment record ID, actual canonical URL, purpose, owner and authorization. Its Pantheon provider resource ID is `SITE_UUID.environment`. The native profile uses that exact combined resource in `config.environment_id`.

Open **Native tools** and select the existing Pantheon provider. Copy `php_path`, `terminus_path` and `site_root` from the successful runtime result into the selected host's native profile. The application retains the target and profile revisions.

The receiver accepts ordinary existing application requests:

~~~bash
python3 "$GOVHUB_CODE/pantheon_receive.py" \
  --runtime-dir "$GOVHUB_RUNTIME" call \
  --workspace "$GOVHUB_STATE" --source-root "$GOVHUB_INPUTS" \
  --username "$GOVHUB_OPERATOR" --password-env GOVHUB_PASSWORD \
  operations.configure --request "$GOVHUB_REQUESTS/profile.json"
~~~

`profile.json` is the original `operations.configure` payload: `{environment_id, expected_revision, config}`. Use the actual current record revision and full schema-supported profile. The receiver confirms that the two executable paths name the prepared PHP/Terminus installation.

For operating records, use the same `data`, `expected_revision`, `note` and `archived` payload used by the browser:

~~~bash
python3 "$GOVHUB_CODE/pantheon_receive.py" \
  --runtime-dir "$GOVHUB_RUNTIME" record \
  --workspace "$GOVHUB_STATE" --source-root "$GOVHUB_INPUTS" \
  --username "$GOVHUB_OPERATOR" --password-env GOVHUB_PASSWORD \
  environments "$GOVHUB_ENVIRONMENT_RECORD" \
  --request "$GOVHUB_REQUESTS/environment.json"
~~~

A newly selected record uses its chosen original application ID and a null prior revision; an edit uses that same record's returned current revision. Referenced site, agency and owner records must already exist as required by the application's schema.

Run `operations.capabilities` with the selected environment record ID to read native inventory. Its complete response includes the actual profile/schema, native target fingerprint, selected backup names, allowed actions, environment population and reviewed promotion-source code-log SHA-256. The receiver passes the current schema and revision controls through unchanged.

## 5. Operate the complete native journey

`call ACTION --request FILE` sends the complete original JSON payload directly to the existing application. Each result is saved in the private receiving directory with the original request bytes' identity and decoded payload. The application's request key and actor remain the authority for an idempotent operation retry.

Use the current browser form or a request produced from its actual observed records. The operation queue retains the current target/profile revisions, selected cohort, source snapshot, authorization and explicit native action.

| Journey | Existing action and native choice | Original source used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source inventory | `sources.capture` / `pantheon-capture` | Actual selected site's environment, code and backup catalog |
| Complete new backup | `operations.create`, type `BACKUP_CREATE`, `pantheon-backup-create` | One original native backup workflow and its exact new code/database/files names |
| Selected backup download | `operations.create`, type `BACKUP_DOWNLOAD`, `pantheon-backup-download` | Explicit filenames selected from the native catalog |
| Rehearsal | `operations.create`, type `REHEARSAL`, selected native action | Original baseline and designated rehearsal target |
| Code promotion | `pantheon-deploy` | Reviewed Dev code for Test, reviewed Test code for Live |
| Full content copy | `pantheon-sync-content` | Same-site explicit source; original files and database steps |
| Component copy | `pantheon-sync-files` or `pantheon-sync-database` | That selected native component only |
| Exact restore | `pantheon-restore` | Original component filenames and matching retained archive bytes |
| Cutover | `operations.create`, type `CUTOVER`, selected native action | Current candidate, comparison and original review |
| Rollback | `operations.create`, type `ROLLBACK`, selected native action | Original baseline and selected exact recovery material |

The complete provider behavior and native source fields are in `PANTHEON.md`. Backup catalog size is native rounded display text; exact archive lengths and SHA-256 values come from the downloaded bytes. Retain all three components. Target-changing operations create and retain their own complete pre-change backup.

Run the selected original request and let the existing queue follow accepted workflows:

~~~bash
python3 "$GOVHUB_CODE/pantheon_receive.py" \
  --runtime-dir "$GOVHUB_RUNTIME" call \
  --workspace "$GOVHUB_STATE" --source-root "$GOVHUB_INPUTS" \
  --username "$GOVHUB_OPERATOR" --password-env GOVHUB_PASSWORD \
  operations.create --request "$GOVHUB_REQUESTS/selected-operation.json" --work
~~~

The existing `cli.run_worker` acquires the application's single service lease. It operates the original queue and keeps a pollable accepted workflow in that queue until its native result settles. If the original browser service already owns the queue, send the request through that service or run `call` without `--work` and use `status` to observe the existing worker.

To continue a queue whose original service has stopped:

~~~bash
python3 "$GOVHUB_CODE/pantheon_receive.py" \
  --runtime-dir "$GOVHUB_RUNTIME" work \
  --workspace "$GOVHUB_STATE" --source-root "$GOVHUB_INPUTS" \
  --username "$GOVHUB_OPERATOR" --password-env GOVHUB_PASSWORD
~~~

This uses the application's service lease, native checkpoints and command ownership. Native work stays in the original operation directory.

## 6. Continue an original workflow or selected backup set

Read the existing operation by its returned application ID:

~~~bash
python3 "$GOVHUB_CODE/pantheon_receive.py" \
  --runtime-dir "$GOVHUB_RUNTIME" status \
  --workspace "$GOVHUB_STATE" --source-root "$GOVHUB_INPUTS" \
  --username "$GOVHUB_OPERATOR" --password-env GOVHUB_PASSWORD \
  "$GOVHUB_OPERATION_ID" --wait-seconds 300
~~~

`status` is an observation command. It follows the existing worker's operation, emits changes in the retained operation revision, and saves the complete final operation/events/files response. A returned `active: true` means the selected operation is still queued, running or following its actual accepted native workflow.

When the existing operation requests an explicit association after a lost native response, send its original continuation through `operations.resume`. The full payload uses:

- Existing `operation_id` and current `expected_revision`.
- A distinct request key for this actual continuation and the operating reason.
- `native_workflow_id` plus `native_workflow_step` for the current pending step.
- Or `native_backup_files` containing exact `code`, `database` and `files` names, plus `native_backup_step`, for the pending original backup set.

A successful native bridge dispatch first retains its real workflow UUID in a sidecar, then its original receipt. The provider consumes that original result after process-output loss and inspects the same workflow. Manual UUID selection is for an unresolved original association; the provider validates the step, target, immutable UUID and pre-command workflow population.

~~~bash
python3 "$GOVHUB_CODE/pantheon_receive.py" \
  --runtime-dir "$GOVHUB_RUNTIME" call \
  --workspace "$GOVHUB_STATE" --source-root "$GOVHUB_INPUTS" \
  --username "$GOVHUB_OPERATOR" --password-env GOVHUB_PASSWORD \
  operations.resume --request "$GOVHUB_REQUESTS/original-continuation.json" --work
~~~

A completed native cohort action advances to its actual observation step. Retain the native execution capture and real `RESTORED` six-column inventory, accept it through the existing intake, then call `operations.observe` with the original operation/revision and returned source IDs. The existing comparator retains the final differences and state.

Current operating references should always come from the returned source and application records. Restoring a component, promoting code, or copying content remains an actual selected provider action with its original source and target.

## 8. Deliver, back up and cold-reopen

Create the complete handover through `exports.create` or the **Complete handover** form. Select the actual plans and any completed content/visitor records; include original sources. The existing export captures its original source versions, operating requests, selected native files, observations, reviews and complete output population.

Select its returned export ID and two new absolute destinations:

~~~bash
python3 "$GOVHUB_CODE/pantheon_receive.py" \
  --runtime-dir "$GOVHUB_RUNTIME" handover \
  --workspace "$GOVHUB_STATE" --source-root "$GOVHUB_INPUTS" \
  --username "$GOVHUB_OPERATOR" --password-env GOVHUB_PASSWORD \
  --export-id "$GOVHUB_EXPORT_ID" \
  --destination "$GOVHUB_DELIVERY" --backup "$GOVHUB_RECEIVED_STATE"
~~~

The receiver uses the existing `cli.export_files` to copy and rehash every original handover file. It invokes the application's coherent native-storage backup, then starts a fresh Python process to authenticate and open the copied workspace. It compares the original workspace identity and complete retained operation population before returning `state: RECEIVED`. The cold reopen keeps the explicitly selected external `GOVHUB_INPUTS` directory. Before copying, the receiver rejects delivery or backup destinations that contain that intake or sit inside it. On another host, select that host's actual separate intake directory; the original private sources remain in the received workspace.

The application's backup lease keeps the copied native journals in the same database generation. Complete the original active native write before copying that generation. Existing `TRANSFER_INCOMPLETE` or `BACKUP_INCOMPLETE` markers identify an interrupted original transfer; retain their directories and inspect the original copy result before selecting a new delivery destination.

The complete editable backup carries the database, retained sources, staff credentials, reconciliation key, native command/result files and original relocation metadata. The full application source package accompanies it. Native account credentials remain with the designated receiving host; the original Terminus session and target are explicitly selected there.

A receiving host with different PHP/Terminus paths first runs `prepare`. The provider's `operations.resume` and read-only `operations.capabilities` accept `runtime_bindings: {php_path, terminus_path, site_root}` separately from the original profile and business intent. The receiver can add exactly the prepared values to the selected original request:

~~~bash
python3 "$GOVHUB_CODE/pantheon_receive.py" \
  --runtime-dir "$GOVHUB_RUNTIME" call \
  --workspace "$GOVHUB_RECEIVED_STATE" \
  --source-root "$GOVHUB_INPUTS" \
  --username "$GOVHUB_OPERATOR" --password-env GOVHUB_PASSWORD \
  operations.resume --request "$GOVHUB_REQUESTS/receiving-continuation.json" \
  --bind-runtime --work
~~~

The request keeps its original operation ID, expected revision, reason and continuation request key. Add its exact workflow/step or backup selection when the current operation requires it. `--bind-runtime` attaches the three prepared native paths and records both the original request and applied payload, together with the prepared runtime file's identity. It rejects a conflicting explicit binding. It also works with `operations.capabilities` for a receiving-host observation.

The selected site, environment, reviewed source, original intent, received workflow UUID and prior command records remain attached to the same operation. An ordinary new operation uses the current configured runtime profile. Inspect the same operation after reopening before resuming it.

## Receiving completion

The useful receiving result consists of the exact source/package identity, actual native CLI/plugin identity, original workspace/actor, selected account/site/environment, completed or retained provider operation, native backup/file identities, restored observation, browser URL and complete exported/received workspace. Each item comes from the original corresponding operation.

Setup and intake result files remain private under `GOVHUB_RUNTIME`. Provider command records and outputs remain in the original GovHub workspace, so its native artifact retention and complete handover carry them to the next operating engineer.

## Continue an interrupted receiving handover

The original `handover` command records one exact receiving intent under
`<runtime-dir>/handovers/<intent-sha256>/state.json`. The intent binds the
original workspace, staff actor, retained export ID and file hashes, separate
intake directory, export destination and private backup destination. A native
receiving lease serializes the copy and cold-reopen phases on that runtime.

If a command returns an error or its caller is lost, retain its original
command record and use the **same** command and paths with `--resume`:

~~~sh
python3 -B /absolute/application/workspace/pantheon_receive.py \
  --runtime-dir /absolute/private-runtime \
  handover \
  --workspace /absolute/accepted-workspace \
  --source-root /absolute/external-intake \
  --username original-admin \
  --password-env ORIGINAL_PRIVATE_PASSWORD_ENV \
  --export-id original-retained-export-id \
  --destination /absolute/customer-handover \
  --backup /absolute/customer-workspace \
  --resume
~~~

Resume first verifies the existing original export and private backup. A
complete export must have the exact retained member collection, lengths and
SHA-256 values. A complete backup must retain its original workspace identity,
a readable consistent SQLite database, all referenced immutable source blobs,
the original reconciliation identity and every declared native-history file.
The original operation population must still match the first receiving intent.

A verified complete phase is adopted without another export or backup call.
An incomplete phase remains intact at an adjacent
`<destination>.interrupted-<id>` path; the journal records its original and
retained locations, exact file hashes and modes before the same-filesystem
rename. The original create-only export or backup API can then finish a new
copy at the same selected destination. No old incomplete marker, command
record or native provider result is discarded. If a completed phase's files
later differ, the receiver stops for reconciliation instead of replacing them.

The existing cold-reopen command then authenticates and opens the copied
workspace without starting its provider worker. A successful retained
cold-reopen output is verified and reused after caller loss. Earlier failed or
interrupted read records remain beside the necessary new local reopen. The
receiver checks the original workspace identity and native operation
population before committing `RECEIVED`. Reopening a completed receiving
intent preserves its first completion time and returns its retained result.

# Multi-site cutover operations

A complete local operating workspace for the original GovHub cutover audit. Staff retain original inventories and native material, prepare explicit migration cohorts, review exact source changes, operate an actual Drupal or Acquia target, reconcile the restored observation and deliver a complete successor handover.

The application has a Python service, an industrial browser interface, a terminal operator and a durable native worker. Its state lives in a private SQLite database with content-addressed source files. The original six-column comparison engine in `../cutover.py` remains unchanged.

## Open the workspace

Use Python 3.11 or newer on Linux or macOS and a current browser. The operating workspace itself uses the Python standard library. Native Drupal work uses the PHP, Drush, database access and site configuration already installed on the selected host. Acquia work uses the published Cloud API and a token supplied through an environment variable.

Keep these paths separate:

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Application directory | This `workspace` directory, its unchanged vendor core, and the adjacent original `cutover.py` |
| Private workspace directory | Database, retained source versions, native results, staff credentials and handovers |
| Original input directory | Files supplied by the actual source operator, including large native backups |
| Backup or delivery directory | A new destination for an explicitly requested complete transfer |

Run the following from this application directory, substituting the operator's absolute paths. Initialization prompts for a new administrator password.

```bash
python3 cli.py \
  --workspace /srv/govhub/state \
  --source-root /srv/govhub/inputs \
  --username operations-admin \
  init --name "GovHub cutover operations" --mode SUPPLIED

python3 server.py \
  --workspace /srv/govhub/state \
  --source-root /srv/govhub/inputs \
  --port 8792
```

Open the local URL printed by the service. The service binds to `127.0.0.1`. It verifies the request host and origin, uses opaque authenticated sessions, and starts the same durable native worker used by the terminal operator. Starting a second service for the same workspace returns its existing ownership conflict.

Use `PILOT` at initialization for an operator's isolated rehearsal. The selected input mode remains visible in the workspace and retained outputs. It is separate from the source observation, environment identity and actual native execution.

The default assessment core is supplied under `vendor/assessment-core`. To compose a separately installed copy of the exact original core, use `--assessment-core /absolute/core/path` or `GOVHUB_ASSESSMENT_CORE`. The vendor guide records its source identities.

```csv
agency_id,canonical_url,export_sha256,backup_sha256,route_count,observed_http_status
```

## Prepare and review a migration cohort

Create a cohort from one baseline and one candidate snapshot. Enter the explicit comparison IDs, minimum baseline coverage, accountable owner, operating window, rollback instruction and relevant context.

**Run source audit** invokes the unchanged `cutover.audit(before, after, approvals, min_agencies)`. The native audit retains:

* Unpaired source sites.
* Canonical URL, export hash, backup hash and route-count differences.
* The candidate's observed HTTP status.
* Minimum baseline coverage.
* Exact field approvals and any stale or mismatched decisions.

The workspace separately checks that every declared comparison ID occurs in the selected sources. Its combined source status passes when the original audit and the explicit cohort scope both pass.

A reviewer can retain a decision for an exact observed field change. That decision records the original comparison ID, field, before and after values, reason, author and cohort revision. Saving it reruns the source audit. A revocation retains the original decision and records the reason for withdrawing its applicability.

The reviewer then retains **Approve** or **Return** against the current audited cohort revision. Approval requires the current successful audit. Revising the cohort preserves its previous source pair, audits and review, then requires a decision for the new operating revision. Earlier exact field decisions are applicable only when the same source values still match.

The plan history and audit history remain available beside the current operating record.

# Skpr operating project

The Skpr provider runs the released native CLI inside the existing GovHub workspace. It supplies environment and release discovery, complete source capture, native backup creation and download, a reviewed restore or deployment, and a receiving command that opens the complete delivered application and the same saved operating project.

The original GovHub records, source cohorts, staff accounts, native worker, revision controls, comparison inventory, exports and private workspace backup remain the operating system for this work. Skpr credentials stay with the existing native account on the operating host.

## Native source and runtime

The supported CLI is **Skpr v1.9.4**, original source commit **0014e431f5892591fb04600a2e2ca706d70a3897**. Its API dependency is **v1.8.5**, source commit **93f97034c4f88cb29d369f03761c12599f63b92c**.

The receiving host can select an existing native executable or receive the original Linux amd64 release archive:

| Original dependency | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Release | [Skpr CLI v1.9.4](https://github.com/skpr/cli/releases/tag/v1.9.4) |
| Archive | [skpr_1.9.4_linux_amd64.tar.gz](https://github.com/skpr/cli/releases/download/v1.9.4/skpr_1.9.4_linux_amd64.tar.gz) |
| Bytes | 45,368,316 |
| SHA-256 | e9ede2b799e9a32bae51446da404c10467df252a4d844efd2f166fa54205bd58 |
| API source | [skpr/api at the original API commit](https://github.com/skpr/api/tree/93f97034c4f88cb29d369f03761c12599f63b92c) |

| Receiving application | skpr_receive.py |

This application invokes the original release as an external dependency. The Skpr CLI source has not been copied into the application. The source references below identify the command and data contracts used by the integration.

The host needs Python 3.11 or later, its existing Git and POSIX env executables, the original project containing .skpr/config.yml, and the existing Skpr login. Native backup downloads also use the restic executable and mounted original repository provided within the Skpr environment.

Skpr reads .skpr/config.yml from its original project context and then applies SKPR_API, SKPR_SSH and SKPR_PROJECT. The adapter binds those three public target values for each child process. The native account retains SKPR_USERNAME, SKPR_PASSWORD, SKPR_SESSION or its existing cached login through the released CLI. The application does not copy their values into the profile.

## Prepare the operating host

Choose the actual cluster hostname, project and environment. The native environment identity is their exact slash-separated value:


The same value belongs in the GovHub environment record's provider resource and the native profile. Source backups may come from another environment in the same selected project.

~~~sh
python3 skpr_receive.py --runtime-dir "$SKPR_RECEIVING_DIRECTORY" prepare \
~~~

Alternatively, replace --skpr with --archive and the complete original release archive path. The archive receiver verifies its full byte count and SHA-256 before retaining the executable. Existing runtime selection is also tied to the actual executable hash and its native --version output.

The preparation result includes the four receiving path fields: skpr_path, git_path, env_path and site_root. Save those values in the Skpr native profile. Select existing command paths; keep the private operating directory separate from the site source.

Open the original application using its existing workspace, separate source intake, staff username and password environment-variable name:

## Complete source capture

Start **Capture original source** from the native environment or operating queue. The operation retains:

- The native CLI version and executable identity.
- The complete original environment, backup, restore, component and release observations.
- Every regular .skpr file with its original relative path, bytes, hash and mode.
- The original Git commit and a Git bundle containing its reachable refs and HEAD.
- A tracked source archive for the exact commit.
- Separate staged and unstaged binary patches, their combined patch, and original porcelain status.
- An archive of the original untracked, nonignored source files.
- The mounted restic repository's complete native snapshot catalogue.
- Original command arguments, output, exit state and the source package manifest.

The source package retains Git-managed dependency declarations and lock files. Native dependency installation and project build follow the received site's original instructions. The original .skpr directory is captured in full even when a file there is ignored by Git.

Source capture checks the commit, status, index, working patch, untracked file bodies and configuration after the full capture. A receiving operation therefore opens one coherent captured source state. If the site is being edited during capture, finish that edit and capture the resulting source as a new original source observation.

The private GovHub workspace must be outside the original project source directory. Its credential-bearing configuration, provider metadata and backup files belong in the private project handover.

## Native backup creation and lifecycle

**Create and retain native backup** submits the original environment backup command. An optional JSON array of native MySQL policy names supplies the CLI's --mysql-policy values. An empty array uses the environment's actual native policy.

The command immediately returns the original backup name. The saved operation retains that name and observes the same item in the native backup collection until its phase is Completed. It retains native Failed or Unknown phases as the returned provider outcome. Normal accepted work is polled at 15-second intervals; an interrupted provider read can use the longer retained continuation interval.

The environment backup and component records use different identifiers:

| Native collection | Exact parent relationship |
| --- | --- |
| Environment backup | BackupStatus.Name is the whole backup's identity |
| MySQL component | MySQLBackupStatus.BackupID equals the parent environment backup's Name |
| Volume component | VolumeBackupStatus.BackupID equals the parent environment backup's Name |
| Restore | RestoreStatus.Backup identifies the selected original environment backup |

A component's Name identifies that component record. Its Database or Volume contains the native physical resource. The whole backup's Databases and Volumes describe its logical resource collection. The adapter retains those values separately and joins only through the original BackupID relationship.

The released CLI prints a specific English empty-collection response when no backup or restore exists. Those exact empty results are parsed as an empty original collection. The native n/a component placeholder is also handled explicitly.

Completed backup component counts and phases are checked against the whole backup's original databases and volumes before download. The application retains the backup's original policy context so that the delivered recovery set reflects what the native backup actually contains.

## Retain the actual backup archives

Skpr exposes the original mounted restic repository within the environment. The operator downloads a selected backup through that repository:

~~~text
skpr exec ENVIRONMENT -- restic snapshots --json
skpr exec ENVIRONMENT -- restic ls --json FULL_SNAPSHOT_ID
skpr exec ENVIRONMENT -- restic dump -a tar FULL_SNAPSHOT_ID /
~~~

The released SSH implementation joins its remote arguments before execution. The adapter quotes each original argument once before handing it to that native command.

When the native backup is ready, the saved operation displays every original database and volume component and the complete mounted snapshot catalogue. Choose the actual full snapshot ID for each component. Search uses original snapshot ID, time, hostname, tags and paths. The selections stay on this same operation and are exported with the backup manifest.

The environment backup's Name, the component Name and the restic snapshot ID are retained as separate fields. A selected restic ID must occur in the current native repository catalogue. A full snapshot may intentionally serve several selected components; its archive is downloaded once, and every component association is preserved.

Each download retains the complete native file listing, original tar archive, whole-archive hash, and an index with every member's path, type, size and body hash. Hard links retain their native target and resolved file identity. The received file inventory must agree with the selected snapshot's original listing.

The individual artifact allowance defaults to 1 GiB and can be raised for the actual project. The native file listing is checked before a large archive download. Archive source bodies are streamed and hashed rather than embedded into the operation's small saved checkpoint.

**Download selected native backup** uses the exact Name selected in the profile. Backup selection buttons fill the original identity and source environment. Save the profile to retain that choice.

## Reviewed restore and deployment

Create the original comparison cohort and bind the captured source, selected native backup manifest and retained original files through GovHub's existing Sources and Inventory workflow. The restore manifest's native format is **skpr-backup-manifest**.

A rehearsal, cutover or rollback uses the existing source pins, actual environment record and operating authorization reference. The provider supplies two actions:

| Action | Native operation |
| --- | --- |
| skpr-restore | Restore the selected original environment backup to this configured environment |
| skpr-deploy | Deploy the existing reviewed release with the captured original .skpr configuration |

Both journeys first create and retain a native backup of the target environment. The recovery backup's actual archive set remains on the same original operation. For restore, the reviewed source backup archives are also received before the target change.

Restore uses the released command:

~~~text
skpr restore create TARGET_ENVIRONMENT ORIGINAL_BACKUP_NAME --force
~~~

The application observes the original returned restore ID and checks that the native result names the reviewed backup. A backup from another environment in the same Skpr project is supported through source_environment. The retained source manifest must identify that exact cluster, project, source environment and backup.

Deployment uses:

~~~text
skpr deploy ENVIRONMENT EXISTING_RELEASE_VERSION
~~~

The original CLI loads the site's .skpr configuration and performs its native validation. Its warnings and violations remain in the original output. The adapter uses the normal released deployment command.

Skpr's deployment command returns a streamed update rather than a separate job ID. The adapter retains the original command process and stream and observes the environment's Deployed phase, selected release version and image identity. If a stream is interrupted during a same-version deployment, the original native command history remains the continuation context.

After a target change completes, GovHub accepts the actual restored source observation through the existing six-column inventory comparison. The same original operation retains its source, recovery backup, native output and observed final result.

The existing worker reopens the retained operation and command journals. Successful commands reuse their original verified output; provider writes retain their original native request identity. A failed read can run a new read attempt with its previous output preserved.

When a provider response was lost after a command started, **Original Skpr request** accepts the actual backup or restore ID from that original native work. The adapter checks the original target, request purpose and pre-request catalogue. A supplied ID that already existed before that command cannot replace the operation's request.

When moving to a different operating host, **Receiving machine** supplies only these local bindings:

~~~json
{

}
~~~

These paths refer to the current receiving machine. The operation's cluster, project, environment, reviewed source, native ID and deployment intent stay attached to their original saved instruction.

The receiver can attach its prepared runtime to the original GovHub continuation JSON:

# Static releases

Use the original GovHub workspace to retain a complete Tome build, compare it with the selected local release, review every changed path, and publish through the existing worker. Each output edition keeps the original generated files and their byte counts, SHA-256 values, build report, source inputs and native operation identity. Release operations retain the selected target, comparison, review and predecessor so an interrupted publication can be reconciled and an earlier release can be selected deliberately.

Open **Static releases** in the existing application (`#static`). The original environment records, native configuration, build pages, operation history and workspace backup remain part of the same application.

## Start with the original complete build

Use the existing environment and native profile with `source_kind: tome`. Complete its original **CAPTURE** operation, then select that operation when retaining an output edition. A failed Tome command, incomplete native result or missing generated file prevents a complete edition from being created.

The receiver requires exactly one original static build report and the complete matching `static_asset` inventory. Each report path must identify one retained file with the same original path, byte count and SHA-256. Repeated paths, missing assets and additional unreported assets are errors. Retaining the same completed operation and report again returns the original edition.

Open the retained edition at `#static-edition?id=EDITION_ID`. Inspect its file count, total bytes, production URI, generator, source inputs and original build identity. Page or search the inventory to inspect individual paths. Inventory paging does not reduce the edition: publication and export use the complete retained set.

A build edition is immutable. To deliver changed generated content, complete another native capture and retain its new edition. Keep the earlier edition because it supplies the comparison and recovery history.

## Configure the actual local target

Create a target from `#static-target-new`, using the original environment and an existing absolute release directory on the machine that runs the worker. Select the ordinary filename used for its current-release symlink, usually `current`. The selected directory must be separate from the private workspace and its ancestors.

The target records the environment identity, absolute directory, filesystem identity and current-pointer name. Those bindings remain fixed. Label and notes have retained revisions and can be edited at `#static-target-edit`. Configure a separate target when the receiving location changes; changing a label does not relocate a release.

Open `#static-target?id=TARGET_ID` and inspect the actual target before preparing a release:

| Observed state | Required continuation |
| --- | --- |
| Current symlink absent | Configure the target without a baseline. The first comparison treats the candidate files as additions. |
| Current symlink present | Select an exact retained baseline edition from the same environment. The complete current tree must match every baseline path, size and hash before it is adopted. |
| Current path is unsuitable, resolves differently, or its contents do not match the selected baseline | Resolve the actual target or select the correct original baseline before proceeding. An unmatched existing tree is not silently adopted or replaced. |
| Another active operation belongs to this target | Continue, inspect or cancel that original operation through the existing operation controls. |

An existing release is adopted only after its complete bytes match the selected baseline. Its current pointer and baseline become the initial retained release. The application does not infer a baseline from a partial directory listing or from the candidate you intend to publish.

## Compare and review the complete output

Choose the retained candidate from the target's original environment and create a comparison against the target's current retained release. Give the plan a useful label and record the reason for the change.

Open `#static-plan?id=PLAN_ID`. The plan binds the exact target revision, candidate, baseline, current release and comparison hash. Inspect the full counts and browse the paths using `all`, `added`, `removed`, `changed` and `unchanged` filters. Review removals as well as changed pages: publication selects the entire candidate tree, so a baseline file absent from the candidate is absent from the new selected release.

Retain the existing review decision, **APPROVE** or **RETURN**, with its reason. The review identifies the exact plan and comparison SHA-256. This is the application's original release review, using its existing account roles. A Return decision keeps the plan and comments available for correction. A later candidate or changed target needs a comparison against the actual current state.

If the page reports that the plan is no longer current, reopen the target and create the appropriate new comparison. The old plan remains a useful historical record; its review does not authorize publication against a different baseline.

## Stage, publish and inspect the result

Stage the selected plan with an operating reason. The original worker creates the complete immutable candidate output under the configured target and verifies the staged files. Staging leaves the current symlink unchanged. Its retained stage record is attached to the original plan.

After the complete comparison is approved and staging has completed, publish that same plan. Use the original operation page (`#static-operation?id=OPERATION_ID`) to follow progress, the native result and retained files. Closing the page does not create a replacement operation or change the worker's ownership.

Publication verifies the configured target and its previous selection, retains the immutable release intent, and atomically replaces the current symlink. It then verifies the selected complete tree and records the release and native receipt. The receipt identifies the target, edition, manifest, plan, review, predecessor and actual selected pointer.

A successful release is established by the original completed operation and the selected target readback. Reopen the target to inspect its current release and release history. Keep the operation ID with the handoff so another operator can recover the exact result rather than repeat a publication from memory.

The output is a local filesystem release. Any web server that serves that current path remains configured through its existing operating arrangement. This workflow does not perform an external CDN deployment or restore a Drupal database.

## Roll back the retained predecessor

From the current target, choose rollback when the current retained release has a predecessor. The operation selects that exact predecessor's complete edition, verifies its files, and retains a new operation and release record. Supply the operating reason and follow the original worker through completion.

Rollback moves the current symlink to the retained predecessor. It preserves the newer immutable edition and its history. It does not delete generated files, rebuild an old site, choose an arbitrary older folder or restore database content. Reopen the target after completion and verify the selected release and predecessor chain.

## Recover the original action

The browser retains each action's stable UUID, action name and exact body in IndexedDB, scoped to the current account and workspace, before submitting it. A completed response is retained before navigation. Use **Recover original action** for an uncertain response and **Open saved result** when the action succeeded but opening or refreshing the next page failed.

Keep the same action identity and body during recovery. Request replay returns the recorded result for that original request before treating later revision changes as a new action. Editing the body belongs to a separate intentional action after the earlier outcome has been resolved.

The original operation controls own cancellation and resumption. A cancellation request is not itself evidence that a symlink was never changed. Once pointer replacement may have been attempted, the worker first reconciles the retained publication intent with the actual exact pointer. It records an already-performed publication before acting on cancellation or changed-current context. This prevents an interrupted successful release from being repeated or misreported as an untouched cancellation.

Use the existing operation's status, cancel and resume controls. Preserve its ID, native checkpoints, retained source and target binding. Do not launch another worker to reinterpret an uncertain publication.

| Situation | Original recovery path |
| --- | --- |
| Response lost after submitting an action | Look up the original request or recover its exact retained envelope. |
| Action completed, next page failed to open | Open its saved result; do not submit the action again. |
| Worker stopped while staging | Inspect and resume the same operation through the existing worker controls. |
| Worker stopped near current-pointer replacement | Let the same operation reconcile its retained intent and actual pointer before another action. |
| Target or current selection changed before publication | Read the original operation outcome, reopen the current target, and prepare a new comparison when required. |
| Local JSON or download publication failed | Recover the original native request/result, then write the returned file to a new output path. |

## Credentials and native host

Set exactly one environment-variable **name** in the profile:

- **api_token_env** names an existing API-token variable. Immediately before an actual request, the provider exchanges its value at the published OAuth endpoint using grant_type=api_token and Basic client platform-api-user:. The access token stays in process memory.
- **access_token_env** names an existing short-lived bearer-token variable. Its value is used directly.

Profiles and source journals retain names rather than token values. No credential enters an API URL, operation body, command-line argument or source artifact. OAuth response bodies contain credentials and stay in memory; nonsecret status, expiry and reference are retained. A 401 never silently repeats a content-changing POST.

**site_root** is the existing absolute native source directory. **git_path**, **upsun_path**, **ssh_path** and **rsync_path** select actual installed executables, by absolute path or a command name resolved on the original native host. See **UPSUN_SOURCE.md** for the complete native source receiver and its exact commands. The API-token reference is mapped to the CLI's expected variable inside its child process.

The runtime binding set is declared by provider_schema().runtime_fields. The provider checks the resource's original HAL action link before a mutation. Missing native capability is reported with the actual resource; no alternate route is invented.

### Branch, synchronize and resource options

Branch requires branch_name, branch_title, branch_type and source_revision. Type is development or staging. clone_parent is explicit. An existing name is not overwritten or silently adopted by a new request; continue its retained original operation or select that environment.

For synchronize or merge, parent_environment_id must match the actual current parent. Synchronization requires at least one code, data or resources selection. Rebase requires code synchronization. Native data synchronization overwrites the child's data.

Optional resources_init is validated against the original action schema:

| Action | Native values |
| --- | --- |
| Branch, activate | default, minimum, parent |
| Merge | child, default, manual, minimum |
| Restore | backup, default, minimum, parent |

Deployment strategy is stopstart by default, matching the released native CLI. Rolling is available only when the actual environment exposes can_rolling_deploy=true. Controlled deploy retains the complete original staged activity set; those activity IDs can legitimately predate this dispatch. Defaults cannot change an already-dispatched request.

### Native snapshots and restore

Native Upsun snapshots remain with the provider. Official support states that they cannot be downloaded, so no upsun-backup-download action is offered. Git/SQL/mount receiving is a separate operation with actual exported bytes.

Backup creation retains every observed before/after snapshot and native activity. **observations.new_backups** is the observed new cohort, not a guessed association with a concurrent snapshot. Select an actual snapshot ID from the native inventory for restore; do not automatically choose a newest or positional row.

Restore requires backup_id from the selected environment, status CREATED, restorable=true, and its complete current detail response. restore_code and restore_resources are explicit. This provider restores to the snapshot's original environment. A code restore compares the resulting actual head with the snapshot's original commit_id.

## Request, response and activity continuity

The existing Session owns private output, events, artifacts, checkpoints, cancellation and process continuation. Before mutation, the provider saves the exact method/path/body and request SHA, reviewed profile/source, full inventory and previous activity/snapshot IDs, and dispatch record.

Every actual API call retains original input, response headers, raw bytes, size/hash, status, timestamps and errors. Completion uses the original declared HTTP body length, including the native pre-read length. A truncated response remains incomplete even if its status began successfully.

The transport does not follow redirects or automatically repeat mutations. Regional HAL references resolve onto the same selected central project authority, matching the original PHP client's authority binding; the original link remains in source. Credentials never go to a response-supplied host.

A complete 429 saves its account deadline and permits the same rejected instruction after that deadline. A 5xx or lost/ambiguous mutation reply keeps uncertainty and requires its original activity; no second POST occurs. A complete 4xx rejection becomes a retained terminal native result.

Every returned activity is polled, with project, environment membership and ID checked. The provider waits for the whole set, receives every complete native log, and retains all actual failures. Native documentation says an activity can report success despite a failed deploy command; failed commands remain material failures in the operator result.

### Recover an interrupted original operation

Resume the same GovHub operation. If its original complete response was saved, it is reopened and its full activity list adopted.

Otherwise select the actual **Original activity ID**, or supply **Original activity IDs JSON** for the complete native activity set. The continuation binds the original request SHA, reason, project, environment and action. It rejects unrelated earlier activities and contradictory native parameters. Controlled deploy preserves its entire original already-staged activity cohort, preserving which request parameters the provider exposed and which it did not. This is explicit original-operation association, not mutation replay.

The accepted response's whole activity list cannot be replaced by another single ID. Both **native_resume.activity_ids** and **resume_checkpoint.native_poll.ids** expose it. Cancelling a local wait retains any dispatched remote activity; it does not claim the remote operation was cancelled.

### Restart-safe polling

The saved native resume checkpoint carries `provider_request_not_before` as an absolute Unix timestamp for the request selected by `provider_request_url`. It is the maximum of the actual account deadline and that exact resource deadline. Receivers use this absolute value and the original operation's `next_poll_at`; `poll_after_seconds` is an observed display interval and must not be turned into a new deadline after restarting. Deadlines for unrelated URLs remain separate in `provider_resource_deadlines`.

This module is the source arm of the existing GovHub Upsun provider. It captures the selected original Git project, its current local source changes, one explicitly selected native database and the selected application's writable mounts. ## Original native contract

The implementation was read against **Upsun CLI 5.13.0**, release commit **b23a9b1ba51afe1ab18ff7f8283ead4998aa80ed**, published 2026-09-30. This is the current Upsun CLI repository, including its maintained PHP implementation under `legacy/`; it does not imply a Platform.sh/Fixed account alias.

- [Relationships.php](https://github.com/upsun/cli/blob/b23a9b1ba51afe1ab18ff7f8283ead4998aa80ed/legacy/src/Service/Relationships.php): relationship selectors are native names, or the native name.index selector when multiple endpoints exist. A relationship is not merely a database service label.

- [MountListCommand.php](https://github.com/upsun/cli/blob/b23a9b1ba51afe1ab18ff7f8283ead4998aa80ed/legacy/src/Command/Mount/MountListCommand.php): `--paths` returns native mount paths.

## Provider integration and exact selection

`capture_source(session, provider_inventory, selection)` returns the full source result and adds its complete ZIP and manifest through the caller's existing `Session.add`. There is no second operation queue or native subprocess controller. The provider owns inventory, intent and cloud changes. The source helper uses `Session.command` for each actual Git and CLI command, including complete native stdout/stderr, input identity, timeout, process group and interrupted-command recovery.

Required selections:

| --- | --- |
| `project_id` | Actual Upsun project ID |

The provider's `api_token_env` is an environment **name**. The admitted Python process reads that value only immediately before exec of the original CLI and maps it to `UPSUN_CLI_TOKEN`. The request, command arguments, manifest and source package contain only the name. The ZIP contains an exact manifest, the original provider inventory, complete CLI request records (without credential values), native response headers/body, command argv/stdout/stderr, original deployed app YAML, selected SQL and every mount archive/node manifest.

Each Git repository and initialized submodule retains:

Mount copies use native rsync `--delete` only against this operation's own private mount staging directory, so a resumed copy cannot retain a stale union of files. No remote deletion occurs.
