<?php
/**
 * Capture the actual installed Drupal editorial model and selected content.
 *
 * GOVHUB_EDITORIAL_REQUEST=/absolute/request.json drush php:script /absolute/inventory.php
 * The request identifies environment_ref, output_path, and optional bundle_ids/entity_ids.
 * It reads the existing bootstrapped site and writes one original inventory.
 */
declare(strict_types=1);

function editorialCanonical(mixed $value): mixed {
  if (!is_array($value)) {
    return $value;
  }
  if (!array_is_list($value)) {
    ksort($value, SORT_STRING);
  }
  foreach ($value as $key => $item) {
    $value[$key] = editorialCanonical($item);
  }
  return $value;
}

function editorialJson(mixed $value): string {
  return json_encode(editorialCanonical($value),
    JSON_UNESCAPED_UNICODE | JSON_UNESCAPED_SLASHES | JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
}

try {
  $requestPath = getenv('GOVHUB_EDITORIAL_REQUEST');
  if (!$requestPath || !is_file($requestPath)) {
    throw new RuntimeException('Set GOVHUB_EDITORIAL_REQUEST to the original request JSON file.');
  }
  $requestBytes = file_get_contents($requestPath);
  if ($requestBytes === FALSE) {
    throw new RuntimeException('The original request cannot be read.');
  }
  $request = json_decode($requestBytes, TRUE, 512, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
  if (!is_array($request) || !is_string($request['environment_ref'] ?? NULL) ||
      trim($request['environment_ref']) === '' || !is_string($request['output_path'] ?? NULL)) {
    throw new RuntimeException('Supply the actual environment_ref and absolute output_path.');
  }
  $outputPath = $request['output_path'];
  if (!str_starts_with($outputPath, '/') || !is_dir(dirname($outputPath))) {
    throw new RuntimeException('The output parent must be an existing absolute directory.');
  }
  $requestSha = hash('sha256', $requestBytes);
  if (file_exists($outputPath)) {
    $existingBytes = file_get_contents($outputPath);
    $existing = json_decode($existingBytes, TRUE, 512, JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR);
    if (($existing['schema'] ?? '') !== 'govhub.editorial-inventory.v1' ||
        ($existing['source']['request_sha256'] ?? '') !== $requestSha) {
      throw new RuntimeException('The output belongs to a different original request. Choose a new output for a new observation.');
    }
    fwrite(STDOUT, editorialJson(['state' => 'REOPENED', 'output' => $outputPath,
      'bytes' => strlen($existingBytes), 'sha256' => hash('sha256', $existingBytes)]) . PHP_EOL);
    return;
  }

  $manager = \Drupal::entityTypeManager();
  $allBundles = $manager->getStorage('node_type')->loadMultiple();
  ksort($allBundles, SORT_STRING);
  $selected = $request['bundle_ids'] ?? array_keys($allBundles);
  if (!is_array($selected) || count($selected) !== count(array_unique($selected)) ||
      array_diff($selected, array_keys($allBundles))) {
    throw new RuntimeException('Choose each existing native content type once.');
  }
  sort($selected, SORT_STRING);
  if (!$selected) {
    throw new RuntimeException('Select at least one installed native content type.');
  }

  $storage = \Drupal::service('config.storage');
  $names = ['system.site'];
  foreach (['user.role.', 'workflows.workflow.'] as $prefix) {
    $names = array_merge($names, $storage->listAll($prefix));
  }
  foreach ($selected as $bundleId) {
    $names[] = 'node.type.' . $bundleId;
    foreach (['field.field.node.' . $bundleId . '.', 'core.entity_form_display.node.' . $bundleId . '.',
              'core.entity_view_display.node.' . $bundleId . '.'] as $prefix) {
      $names = array_merge($names, $storage->listAll($prefix));
    }
    $languageName = 'language.content_settings.node.' . $bundleId;
    if ($storage->exists($languageName)) {
      $names[] = $languageName;
    }
    foreach (\Drupal::service('entity_field.manager')->getFieldDefinitions('node', $bundleId) as $fieldName => $field) {
      $storageName = 'field.storage.node.' . $fieldName;
      if ($storage->exists($storageName)) {
        $names[] = $storageName;
      }
    }
  }
  $names = array_values(array_unique($names));
  sort($names, SORT_STRING);
  $originalConfiguration = $storage->readMultiple($names);
  $configuration = [];
  foreach ($names as $name) {
    if (!array_key_exists($name, $originalConfiguration)) {
      throw new RuntimeException('The selected native configuration disappeared: ' . $name);
    }
    $bytes = editorialJson($originalConfiguration[$name]);
    $configuration[] = ['name' => $name, 'bytes' => strlen($bytes),
      'sha256' => hash('sha256', $bytes), 'data_json' => $bytes];
  }

  $bundles = [];
  foreach ($selected as $bundleId) {
    $bundle = $allBundles[$bundleId];
    $display = $manager->getStorage('entity_form_display')->load('node.' . $bundleId . '.default');
    $fields = [];
    foreach (\Drupal::service('entity_field.manager')->getFieldDefinitions('node', $bundleId) as $name => $field) {
      $fields[] = ['name' => $name, 'label' => (string) $field->getLabel(),
        'description' => (string) $field->getDescription(), 'type' => $field->getType(),
        'required' => $field->isRequired(), 'translatable' => $field->isTranslatable(),
        'read_only' => $field->isReadOnly(),
        'cardinality' => $field->getFieldStorageDefinition()->getCardinality(),
        'form_component' => $display ? $display->getComponent($name) : NULL];
    }
    usort($fields, fn(array $a, array $b): int => strcmp($a['name'], $b['name']));
    $bundles[] = ['id' => $bundleId, 'label' => $bundle->label(),
      'description' => (string) $bundle->get('description'), 'fields' => $fields];
  }

  $roles = [];
  foreach ($manager->getStorage('user_role')->loadMultiple() as $role) {
    $permissions = $role->getPermissions();
    sort($permissions, SORT_STRING);
    $roles[] = ['id' => $role->id(), 'label' => $role->label(),
      'admin' => $role->isAdmin(), 'permissions' => $permissions];
  }
  usort($roles, fn(array $a, array $b): int => strcmp($a['id'], $b['id']));
  $workflows = [];
  foreach ($originalConfiguration as $name => $config) {
    if (!str_starts_with($name, 'workflows.workflow.')) {
      continue;
    }
    $nodeBundles = $config['type_settings']['entity_types']['node'] ?? [];
    if ($nodeBundles && !array_intersect($nodeBundles, $selected)) {
      continue;
    }
    $workflows[] = ['id' => $config['id'], 'label' => $config['label'],
      'type' => $config['type'], 'type_settings' => $config['type_settings'] ?? []];
  }
  usort($workflows, fn(array $a, array $b): int => strcmp($a['id'], $b['id']));

  $nodeStorage = $manager->getStorage('node');
  $query = $nodeStorage->getQuery()->accessCheck(FALSE)->condition('type', $selected, 'IN')->sort('nid');
  $explicitIds = $request['entity_ids'] ?? NULL;
  if ($explicitIds !== NULL) {
    if (!is_array($explicitIds) || count($explicitIds) !== count(array_unique($explicitIds)) ||
        array_filter($explicitIds, fn($id): bool => !is_int($id) && !(is_string($id) && ctype_digit($id)))) {
      throw new RuntimeException('entity_ids must contain each original native node ID once.');
    }
    if ($explicitIds) {
      $query->condition('nid', $explicitIds, 'IN');
    }
  }
  $ids = $explicitIds === [] ? [] : array_values($query->execute());
  if ($explicitIds !== NULL && array_diff(array_map('strval', $explicitIds), array_map('strval', $ids))) {
    throw new RuntimeException('One or more selected content IDs are absent from the selected native types.');
  }
  $entities = [];
  foreach (array_chunk($ids, 100) as $chunk) {
    $loaded = $nodeStorage->loadMultiple($chunk);
    foreach ($chunk as $id) {
      if (!isset($loaded[$id])) {
        throw new RuntimeException('Selected content changed during capture: ' . $id);
      }
      $entity = $loaded[$id];
      $path = $entity->toUrl('canonical', ['absolute' => FALSE])->toString();
      $entities[] = ['id' => (string) $entity->id(), 'uuid' => $entity->uuid(),
        'bundle' => $entity->bundle(), 'label' => $entity->label(),
        'revision_id' => (string) $entity->getRevisionId(), 'language' => $entity->language()->getId(),
        'route' => $path, 'published' => $entity->isPublished(),
        'moderation_state' => $entity->hasField('moderation_state') ? $entity->get('moderation_state')->value : NULL];
    }
    $nodeStorage->resetCache($chunk);
  }

  $currentConfiguration = $storage->readMultiple($names);
  if (editorialJson($currentConfiguration) !== editorialJson($originalConfiguration)) {
    throw new RuntimeException('Native configuration changed during this capture. Repeat the same request before publishing an inventory.');
  }
  $baseUrl = \Drupal::request()->getSchemeAndHttpHost() . \Drupal::request()->getBasePath() . '/';
  $result = ['schema' => 'govhub.editorial-inventory.v1',
    'source' => ['site_uuid' => (string) $originalConfiguration['system.site']['uuid'],
      'site_name' => (string) $originalConfiguration['system.site']['name'], 'base_url' => $baseUrl,
      'drupal_version' => \Drupal::VERSION, 'observed_at' => gmdate('Y-m-d\TH:i:s\Z'),
      'environment_ref' => $request['environment_ref'], 'request_sha256' => $requestSha,
      'bundle_ids' => $selected, 'entity_ids' => array_map('strval', $ids),
      'selection' => $explicitIds === NULL ? 'ALL_SELECTED_CONTENT_TYPES' : 'EXPLICIT_NODE_IDS'],
    'bundles' => $bundles, 'roles' => $roles, 'workflows' => $workflows,
    'entities' => $entities, 'configuration' => $configuration];
  $bytes = editorialJson($result) . PHP_EOL;
  $temporary = tempnam(dirname($outputPath), '.editorial-inventory-');
  if ($temporary === FALSE) {
    throw new RuntimeException('Unable to create the original inventory output.');
  }
  chmod($temporary, 0600);
  $handle = fopen($temporary, 'wb');
  if (!$handle || fwrite($handle, $bytes) !== strlen($bytes) || !fflush($handle)) {
    throw new RuntimeException('The native inventory could not be completely written.');
  }
  if (function_exists('fsync')) {
    fsync($handle);
  }
  fclose($handle);
  if (!link($temporary, $outputPath)) {
    throw new RuntimeException('The inventory output was created concurrently. Reopen the same original request.');
  }
  unlink($temporary);
  $temporary = NULL;
  fwrite(STDOUT, editorialJson(['state' => 'CAPTURED', 'output' => $outputPath,
    'bytes' => strlen($bytes), 'sha256' => hash('sha256', $bytes),
    'content_types' => count($bundles), 'entities' => count($entities),
    'configuration_objects' => count($configuration)]) . PHP_EOL);
}
catch (\Throwable $error) {
  if (isset($handle) && is_resource($handle)) {
    fclose($handle);
  }
  if (isset($temporary) && is_string($temporary) && is_file($temporary)) {
    unlink($temporary);
  }
  fwrite(STDERR, editorialJson(['error' => get_class($error), 'message' => $error->getMessage()]) . PHP_EOL);
  exit(1);
}

"""Editorial operating records using GovHub's original storage and native operations."""
from copy import deepcopy
import json
from urllib.parse import urljoin, urlsplit

from govhub import GovHubError, SOURCE, digest, now, packed
from . import model
from .delivery import PlaybookDeliveryMixin


class PlaybookMixin(PlaybookDeliveryMixin):
    def _playbook_inventory(self, db, file_id):
        file = self._file_row(db, file_id)
        original = self._verify_file(file).read_bytes()
        from govhub import json_bytes
        return model.inventory(json_bytes(original)), {k: file[k] for k in ("id", "filename", "bytes", "sha256")}

    def _playbook_current(self, db, entity_id):
        pointer = self._setting(db, "playbook:" + model.identity(entity_id))
        if not pointer:
            raise GovHubError("PLAYBOOK_NOT_FOUND", "The selected editorial playbook does not exist.", 404)
        return self._get(db, "playbook_definition", pointer["version_id"])

    def _playbook_summary(self, db):
        values = []
        for row in db.execute("SELECT key,value FROM govhub_settings WHERE key LIKE 'playbook:%' ORDER BY key"):
            version = self._get(db, "playbook_definition", json.loads(row["value"])["version_id"])
            reviews = self._objects(db, "playbook_review", version["id"])
            receiving = self._objects(db, "playbook_receiving", version["id"])
            definition = version["definition"]
            values.append({"id": version["entity_id"], "version_id": version["id"], "revision": version["revision"],
                           "label": definition["label"], "owner": definition["owner"],
                           "environment_id": definition["environment_id"],
                           "content_types": len(definition["content_types"]), "tasks": len(definition["tasks"]),
                           "review": reviews[-1] if reviews else None,
                           "receiving": [{k: r[k] for k in ("id", "role", "created_at", "summary")} for r in receiving]})
        return {"playbooks": values}

    def _playbook_get(self, payload):
        with self.connect(snapshot=True) as db:
            version = (self._get(db, "playbook_definition", payload["version_id"]) if payload.get("version_id")
                       else self._playbook_current(db, payload.get("playbook_id")))
            inventory, file = self._playbook_inventory(db, version["inventory"]["id"])
            return {"playbook": version, "inventory": inventory, "file": file,
                    "versions": self._objects(db, "playbook_definition", version["entity_id"]),
                    "reviews": self._objects(db, "playbook_review", version["id"]),
                    "receiving": self._objects(db, "playbook_receiving", version["id"])}

    def _playbook_prepare(self, payload):
        with self.connect(snapshot=True) as db:
            native, file = self._playbook_inventory(db, payload.get("inventory_file_id"))
            env = self._record_db(db, "environments", payload.get("environment_id"))
            if env["id"] != native["source"]["environment_ref"]:
                model.fail("PLAYBOOK_TARGET", "Select the inventory's original environment reference.", 409)
            if payload.get("version_id"):
                previous = self._get(db, "playbook_definition", payload["version_id"])
                current = self._playbook_current(db, previous["entity_id"])
                if (current["id"] != previous["id"]
                        or previous["definition"]["environment_id"] != env["id"]):
                    model.fail("PLAYBOOK_REVISION", "Prepare from the current playbook on its original environment.", 409)
                before, _ = self._playbook_inventory(db, previous["inventory"]["id"])
                value, changes = model.revise_definition(previous["definition"], before, native)
                return {"definition": value, "inventory": native, "file": file, "entity_id": previous["entity_id"],
                        "revision": previous["revision"], "previous_version_id": previous["id"],
                        "preparation_changes": changes, "structure_changes": model.compare(previous["definition"], before, native)}
        value = model.suggested_definition(native, model.text(payload.get("label"), "Playbook name"),
                                           model.text(payload.get("owner"), "Publishing owner"), env["id"])
        return {"definition": value, "inventory": native, "file": file}

    def _playbook_bind(self, db, definition, native):
        environment = self._record_db(db, "environments", definition["environment_id"])
        profile = self._config(db, environment["id"])
        bindings = {"environment": environment, "profile_revision": profile["revision"],
                    "cohorts": [], "content_mappings": [], "visitor_sets": []}
        for plan_id in definition["cohort_plan_ids"]:
            plan = self._plan(db, plan_id)
            bindings["cohorts"].append({"id": plan["id"], "revision": plan["revision"],
                                        "baseline_id": plan["baseline_id"], "candidate_id": plan["candidate_id"]})
        for mapping_id in definition["content_mapping_ids"]:
            mapping = self._get(db, "content_mapping", mapping_id)
            family = self._content_family(db, mapping["family_id"])
            if family["environment_id"] != environment["id"]:
                model.fail("PLAYBOOK_CONTENT_TARGET", "Choose content mappings for the selected native environment.", 409)
            bindings["content_mappings"].append({"id": mapping["id"], "sha256": mapping["sha256"],
                                                 "family_id": family["id"], "family_revision": family["revision"]})
        for set_id in sorted({t["visitor_set_version_id"] for t in definition["tasks"] if t["visitor_set_version_id"]}):
            selected = self._get(db, "visitor_set", set_id)
            journeys = {j["id"]: j for j in selected["value"]["journeys"]}
            for task in definition["tasks"]:
                if task["visitor_set_version_id"] != set_id:
                    continue
                issue = model.task_journey_issue(task, native, journeys.get(task["journey_id"]))
                if issue:
                    model.fail("PLAYBOOK_VISITOR_TASK", issue, 409)
            bindings["visitor_sets"].append(selected)
        return bindings

    def _playbook_save(self, payload, actor):
        entity_id = model.identity(payload.get("playbook_id"), "Playbook identifier")
        with self.connect(write=True) as db:
            key, fingerprint, prior = self._request(db, payload, actor)
            if prior:
                return prior
            native, file = self._playbook_inventory(db, payload.get("inventory_file_id"))
            definition = model.definition(payload.get("definition"), native)
            pointer = self._setting(db, "playbook:" + entity_id)
            revision = pointer["revision"] if pointer else 0
            if type(payload.get("expected_revision")) is not int or payload["expected_revision"] != revision:
                model.fail("PLAYBOOK_REVISION", "Open the current playbook revision before saving changes.", 409)
            relink = []
            if pointer:
                previous = self._get(db, "playbook_definition", pointer["version_id"])
                previous_native, _ = self._playbook_inventory(db, previous["inventory"]["id"])
                previous_tasks = {task["id"]: task for task in previous["definition"]["tasks"]}
                for task in definition["tasks"]:
                    before = previous_tasks.get(task["id"])
                    if not before or not task["visitor_set_version_id"]:
                        continue
                    if any(before[key] != task[key] for key in ("visitor_set_version_id", "journey_id")):
                        continue
                    old_intent, new_intent = model.task_intent(before, previous_native), model.task_intent(task, native)
                    changed = sorted(key for key in old_intent if old_intent[key] != new_intent[key])
                    if changed:
                        relink.append({"task_id": task["id"], "previous_set_version_id": task["visitor_set_version_id"],
                                       "previous_journey_id": task["journey_id"], "changed_fields": changed})
                        task["visitor_set_version_id"], task["journey_id"] = "", ""
            bindings = self._playbook_bind(db, definition, native)
            version = self._object(db, "playbook_definition",
                                   {"entity_id": entity_id, "revision": revision + 1, "definition": definition,
                                    "inventory": file, "bindings": bindings, "visitor_relink": relink,
                                    "previous_version_id": pointer["version_id"] if pointer else "",
                                    "change_note": model.text(payload.get("change_note"), "Change note")},
                                   parent=entity_id, actor=actor["name"])
            self._set(db, "playbook:" + entity_id, {"revision": version["revision"], "version_id": version["id"]})
            result = {"playbook": version}
            self._remember(db, key, fingerprint, result, actor)
            self._changed(db, actor, "Editorial playbook saved", "playbook_definition", version["id"])
            return result

    def _playbook_review(self, payload, actor):
        with self.connect(write=True) as db:
            key, fingerprint, prior = self._request(db, payload, actor)
            if prior:
                return prior
            version = self._get(db, "playbook_definition", payload.get("version_id"))
            if version["sha256"] != payload.get("version_sha256"):
                model.fail("PLAYBOOK_REVIEW_VERSION", "Review the exact displayed playbook edition.", 409)
            previous = self._objects(db, "playbook_review", version["id"])
            if type(payload.get("expected_revision")) is not int or payload["expected_revision"] != len(previous):
                model.fail("PLAYBOOK_REVIEW_REVISION", "Open the latest editorial decision before saving.", 409)
            if payload.get("decision") not in ("ACCEPT", "RETURN"):
                model.fail("PLAYBOOK_REVIEW", "Choose ACCEPT or RETURN for the publishing playbook.")
            review = self._object(db, "playbook_review",
                                  {"version_id": version["id"], "version_sha256": version["sha256"],
                                   "revision": len(previous) + 1, "decision": payload["decision"],
                                   "reason": model.text(payload.get("reason"), "Editorial review reason")},
                                  parent=version["id"], actor=actor["name"])
            result = {"review": review}
            self._remember(db, key, fingerprint, result, actor)
            self._changed(db, actor, "Editorial playbook reviewed", "playbook_review", review["id"])
            return result

    def _playbook_link_visitors(self, payload, actor):
        """Create or revise the original visitor records, then bind their exact version."""
        with self.connect(write=True) as db:
            key, fingerprint, prior = self._request(db, payload, actor)
            if prior:
                return prior
            intents = self._objects(db, "playbook_link_intent", key)
            if intents:
                intent = intents[0]
                if intent["fingerprint"] != fingerprint:
                    model.fail("RETRY_CHANGED", "Continue this original visitor-link request unchanged.", 409)
            else:
                version = self._get(db, "playbook_definition", payload.get("version_id"))
                current = self._playbook_current(db, version["entity_id"])
                if current["id"] != version["id"]:
                    model.fail("PLAYBOOK_REVISION", "Open the current playbook before linking its visitor tasks.", 409)
                native, _ = self._playbook_inventory(db, version["inventory"]["id"])
                if not version["definition"]["tasks"]:
                    model.fail("PLAYBOOK_TASK", "Add the named visitor tasks before creating their operating set.")
                entity_id = "editorial-" + digest(version["entity_id"])[:24]
                p = self._setting(db, "visitor.project:" + entity_id)
                base = native["source"]["base_url"]
                origin = urlsplit(base)
                project = {"label": version["definition"]["label"], "base_url": base,
                           "allowed_origins": [origin.scheme + "://" + origin.netloc],
                           "source_reference": version["definition"]["source_reference"]}
                entities = {e["uuid"]: e for e in native["entities"]}
                journeys = []
                for task in version["definition"]["tasks"]:
                    expected = {"status": [200]}
                    if task["entity_uuid"]:
                        expected["heading"] = entities[task["entity_uuid"]]["label"]
                    journeys.append({"id": task["id"], "name": task["name"], "goal": task["goal"],
                                     "audience": task["audience"], "steps": [{"id": "open",
                                     "url": urljoin(base, task["route"]), "label": task["name"],
                                     "expect": expected, "note": task["notes"]}]})
                sets = []
                for offset in range(0, len(journeys), 150):
                    set_id = entity_id + "-" + str(offset // 150 + 1).zfill(3)
                    previous_set = self._setting(db, "visitor.set:" + set_id)
                    sets.append({"entity_id": set_id, "expected_revision": previous_set["revision"] if previous_set else 0,
                                 "value": {"label": version["definition"]["label"] + " / " + str(offset // 150 + 1),
                                           "journeys": journeys[offset:offset + 150],
                                           "source_reference": version["definition"]["source_reference"]}})
                intent = self._object(db, "playbook_link_intent",
                    {"fingerprint": fingerprint, "version": version, "entity_id": entity_id,
                     "project_revision": p["revision"] if p else 0, "project": project, "sets": sets},
                    parent=key, actor=actor["name"])
        # Each original operation records its own request before the next step.
        # Reopening this intent therefore recovers the same records after interruption.
        project = self.dispatch("visitor.projects.save",
                                {"entity_id": intent["entity_id"], "expected_revision": intent["project_revision"],
                                 "value": intent["project"], "request_key": key + ":project",
                                 "change_note": "Publishing playbook visitor source"}, actor)
        selected_sets, task_bindings = [], {}
        for index, selection in enumerate(intent["sets"]):
            selected = self.dispatch("visitor.sets.save",
                                     {**selection, "project_id": intent["entity_id"],
                                      "request_key": key + ":set:" + str(index),
                                      "change_note": "Publishing playbook visitor tasks"}, actor)
            selected_sets.append(selected["set"])
            task_bindings.update({j["id"]: selected["set"]["id"] for j in selected["set"]["value"]["journeys"]})
        version = intent["version"]
        definition = deepcopy(version["definition"])
        for task in definition["tasks"]:
            task["visitor_set_version_id"] = task_bindings[task["id"]]
            task["journey_id"] = task["id"]
        saved = self._playbook_save({"playbook_action": "definitions.save", "playbook_id": version["entity_id"],
                                    "inventory_file_id": version["inventory"]["id"], "definition": definition,
                                    "expected_revision": version["revision"], "request_key": key + ":definition",
                                    "change_note": "Bound original visitor project and task-set edition"}, actor)
        result = {"project": project["project"], "sets": selected_sets, "playbook": saved["playbook"]}
        with self.connect(write=True) as db:
            request, request_fingerprint, existing = self._request(db, payload, actor)
            if existing:
                return existing
            self._remember(db, request, request_fingerprint, result, actor)
            self._changed(db, actor, "Editorial visitor tasks linked", "playbook_definition", saved["playbook"]["id"])
        return result

    def _playbook_receiving(self, payload, actor):
        with self.connect(write=True) as db:
            key, fingerprint, prior = self._request(db, payload, actor)
            if prior:
                return prior
            version = self._get(db, "playbook_definition", payload.get("version_id"))
            definition = version["definition"]
            original, _ = self._playbook_inventory(db, version["inventory"]["id"])
            received, file = self._playbook_inventory(db, payload.get("inventory_file_id"))
            if received["source"]["environment_ref"] != definition["environment_id"]:
                model.fail("PLAYBOOK_RECEIVING_TARGET", "Select the received inventory for the original environment.", 409)
            role = payload.get("role")
            if role not in ("BASELINE", "CANDIDATE", "RESTORED"):
                model.fail("PLAYBOOK_RECEIVING_ROLE", "Choose BASELINE, CANDIDATE or RESTORED.")
            previous = self._objects(db, "playbook_receiving", version["id"])
            if type(payload.get("expected_revision")) is not int or payload["expected_revision"] != len(previous):
                model.fail("PLAYBOOK_RECEIVING_REVISION", "Reopen the current receiving history before saving.", 409)
            continued_from = model.text(payload.get("continued_from", ""), "Previous receiving observation", False)
            if continued_from:
                earlier = self._get(db, "playbook_receiving", continued_from)
                if (earlier["version_id"] != version["id"] or earlier["inventory"]["id"] != file["id"]
                        or earlier["role"] != role):
                    model.fail("PLAYBOOK_RECEIVING_CONTINUATION",
                               "Continue the same edition, inventory and receiving role, or start a new observation.", 409)
            operations = []
            for operation_id in model.ids(payload.get("operation_ids", []), "Native operations"):
                operation = self._operation(db, operation_id)
                if operation["environment_id"] != definition["environment_id"]:
                    model.fail("PLAYBOOK_RECEIVING_TARGET", "Select native operations on the playbook's environment.", 409)
                if operation.get("plan_id") and definition["cohort_plan_ids"] and operation["plan_id"] not in definition["cohort_plan_ids"]:
                    model.fail("PLAYBOOK_RECEIVING_COHORT", "The native operation belongs to a different selected cohort.", 409)
                cohort = next((p for p in version["bindings"]["cohorts"] if p["id"] == operation.get("plan_id")), None)
                if cohort and operation.get("plan_revision") != cohort["revision"]:
                    model.fail("PLAYBOOK_RECEIVING_COHORT", "Use the native operation for this retained cohort edition, or save the revised playbook.", 409)
                if operation.get("content_plan_id") and definition["content_mapping_ids"]:
                    native_plan = self._get(db, "content_plan", operation["content_plan_id"])
                    if native_plan["mapping_id"] not in definition["content_mapping_ids"]:
                        model.fail("PLAYBOOK_RECEIVING_MAPPING", "Select the native operation for an original mapped content edition.", 409)
                operations.append({k: operation.get(k) for k in (
                    "id", "revision", "type", "state", "environment_id", "plan_id", "plan_revision",
                    "content_plan_id", "profile", "actual_started_at", "actual_finished_at", "native_capture_file_id")})
            editor_input = model.indexed(payload.get("editor_decisions", []), "bundle", "Editor receiving decisions")
            bundle_ids = {b["bundle"] for b in definition["content_types"]}
            if set(editor_input) - bundle_ids:
                model.fail("PLAYBOOK_EDITOR", "Record editor receiving against the selected content types.")
            editors, extra_files = [], set()
            for bundle in definition["content_types"]:
                item = editor_input.get(bundle["bundle"])
                if item is None:
                    editors.append({"bundle": bundle["bundle"], "owner": bundle["owner"], "decision": "PENDING",
                                    "reason": "", "files": []})
                    continue
                if item.get("decision") not in ("ACCEPT", "RETURN", "PENDING"):
                    model.fail("PLAYBOOK_EDITOR", "Use ACCEPT, RETURN or PENDING for an editor receiving outcome.")
                files = []
                for file_id in model.ids(item.get("file_ids", []), "Editor receiving files"):
                    metadata = self._file_row(db, file_id)
                    self._verify_file(metadata)
                    files.append({k: metadata[k] for k in ("id", "filename", "sha256", "bytes")})
                    extra_files.add(file_id)
                editors.append({"bundle": bundle["bundle"], "owner": bundle["owner"], "decision": item["decision"],
                                "reason": model.text(item.get("reason", ""), "Editor receiving reason", item["decision"] != "PENDING"),
                                "files": files})
            editions = [self._get(db, "visitor_edition", e) for e in
                        model.ids(payload.get("visitor_edition_ids", []), "Visitor editions")]
            tasks = []
            for task in definition["tasks"]:
                matches = [e for e in editions if e["definition"]["id"] == task["visitor_set_version_id"]]
                if len(matches) > 1:
                    model.fail("PLAYBOOK_VISITOR_EDITION", "Choose one observed edition per original visitor set for this receiving.")
                outcome = {"task_id": task["id"], "name": task["name"], "status": "PENDING",
                           "edition_id": "", "journey_id": task["journey_id"], "result": None, "review": None}
                if matches:
                    selected = matches[0]
                    if digest(packed(selected["result"])) != selected["result_sha256"]:
                        model.fail("PLAYBOOK_VISITOR_SOURCE", "The retained visitor result identity changed.", 409)
                    journey = next((j for j in selected["result"]["journeys"] if j["id"] == task["journey_id"]), None)
                    if journey is None:
                        model.fail("PLAYBOOK_VISITOR_SOURCE", "The captured edition does not contain the selected task.", 409)
                    reviews = self._objects(db, "visitor_review", selected["id"])
                    review = reviews[-1] if reviews else None
                    accepted = bool(review and review["decision"] == "ACCEPT" and
                                    (journey["status"] == "PASS" or any(x["journey_id"] == task["journey_id"]
                                     for x in review.get("exceptions", []))))
                    binding = model.receiving_task_binding(task, original, received, selected)
                    returned = bool(review and review["decision"] == "RETURN")
                    complete = selected["capture_status"] == "COMPLETE" and binding["matched"] and not returned
                    outcome.update(edition_id=selected["id"], result=journey, review=review, binding=binding,
                                   status="ACCEPT" if complete and accepted else
                                   "PASS" if complete and journey["status"] == "PASS" else "RETURN")
                tasks.append(outcome)
            changes = model.compare(definition, original, received)
            accept_changes = payload.get("accept_changes", False)
            if type(accept_changes) is not bool:
                model.fail("PLAYBOOK_CHANGES", "Record whether the observed structural changes are accepted.")
            change_reason = model.text(payload.get("change_reason", ""), "Structural change decision", bool(changes and accept_changes))
            native_complete = bool(operations) and all(o["state"] == "COMPLETE" and o["actual_finished_at"] for o in operations)
            editors_complete = all(e["decision"] == "ACCEPT" for e in editors)
            tasks_complete = bool(tasks) and all(t["status"] in ("PASS", "ACCEPT") for t in tasks)
            editorial_reviews = self._objects(db, "playbook_review", version["id"])
            editorial_review = editorial_reviews[-1] if editorial_reviews else None
            playbook_accepted = bool(editorial_review and editorial_review["decision"] == "ACCEPT")
            summary = {"playbook_accepted": playbook_accepted, "native_complete": native_complete, "editor_accepted": sum(e["decision"] == "ACCEPT" for e in editors),
                       "editor_total": len(editors), "visitor_accepted": sum(t["status"] in ("PASS", "ACCEPT") for t in tasks),
                       "visitor_total": len(tasks), "structural_changes": len(changes),
                       "changes_accepted": accept_changes,
                       "state": "COMPLETE" if playbook_accepted and native_complete and editors_complete and tasks_complete and
                                (not changes or accept_changes) else "IN_PROGRESS"}
            record = self._object(db, "playbook_receiving",
                {"version_id": version["id"], "version_sha256": version["sha256"], "revision": len(previous) + 1,
                 "role": role, "inventory": file, "observed_source": received["source"], "operations": operations,
                 "continued_from": continued_from,
                 "editorial_review": editorial_review,
                 "editors": editors, "visitor_tasks": tasks, "visitor_edition_ids": [e["id"] for e in editions],
                 "changes": changes, "accept_changes": accept_changes, "change_reason": change_reason,
                 "source_file_ids": sorted(extra_files), "summary": summary,
                 "reason": model.text(payload.get("reason"), "Receiving note")},
                parent=version["id"], actor=actor["name"])
            result = {"receiving": record}
            self._remember(db, key, fingerprint, result, actor)
            self._changed(db, actor, "Editorial and visitor receiving retained", "playbook_receiving", record["id"], summary)
            return result

    def _playbook_compare(self, payload):
        with self.connect(snapshot=True) as db:
            version = self._get(db, "playbook_definition", payload.get("version_id"))
            before, original = self._playbook_inventory(db, version["inventory"]["id"])
            after, received = self._playbook_inventory(db, payload.get("inventory_file_id"))
            if after["source"]["environment_ref"] != version["definition"]["environment_id"]:
                model.fail("PLAYBOOK_RECEIVING_TARGET", "Select the inventory for the original environment.", 409)
            return {"changes": model.compare(version["definition"], before, after),
                    "original": original, "received": received,
                    "original_source": before["source"], "received_source": after["source"]}

    def _playbook_dispatch(self, action, payload, actor):
        payload = deepcopy(payload)
        payload["playbook_action"] = action
        if action == "snapshot":
            with self.connect(snapshot=True) as db:
                return self._playbook_summary(db)
        handlers = {"inventories.compare": lambda: self._playbook_compare(payload),
                    "definitions.prepare": lambda: self._playbook_prepare(payload),
                    "definitions.save": lambda: self._playbook_save(payload, actor),
                    "definitions.get": lambda: self._playbook_get(payload),
                    "reviews.save": lambda: self._playbook_review(payload, actor),
                    "visitors.link": lambda: self._playbook_link_visitors(payload, actor),
                    "receiving.save": lambda: self._playbook_receiving(payload, actor)}
        if action == "exports.create":
            payload.pop("playbook_action", None)
            return self._exports_create(payload, actor)
        if action not in handlers:
            model.fail("PLAYBOOK_ACTION", "This editorial playbook operation does not exist.", 404)
        return handlers[action]()

            f("purpose", "Operating purpose", "select", options=["Incumbent", "Candidate", "Rehearsal", "Production"], default="Rehearsal"),
            f("provider_resource_id", "Actual provider environment identifier"),
            f("canonical_url", "Environment HTTPS URL"), f("owner", "Operating owner"),

            f("data_location", "Data location"), f("native_profile", "Configured native driver profile"),
            f("notes", "Runtime, access and scope notes", "textarea"), *review]},
        "migration_issues": {"title": "Migration work", "singular": "Migration issue", "fields": [
            f("name", "Issue or corrective work", required=True),
            f("site_ids", "Affected sites", "references", ref="sites"), f("plan_id", "Plan identifier"),

            f("description", "Observed condition and consequence", "textarea"),
            f("resolution", "Actual corrective action and result", "textarea"),
            f("resolved_at", "Actual completion time", "datetime"), *review]},

        item["govhub"] = True
        item["group"] = "GovHub operations"

    schema.SCHEMAS.update(values)

description: >
  Learn how to use and create contexts in Castor to manage environments,
  variables, and process execution settings for your tasks.
---

# Context

For every task that Castor run, it uses a `Context` object. This object
contains the default values for a bunch of built-in functions like `run()`, `watch()`,
`capture()`, etc.
It configures working directory of the command, environment variables, PTY, TTY,
timeout, etc...

It also contains custom values that can be set by the user and reused in tasks.

The context is immutable, which means that every time you change a value, a new
context is created.

## Using the context

### The `context()` function

You can get the initial context thanks to the `context()` function:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\context;
use function Castor\io;
use function Castor\run;

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    $context = context();

    io()->writeln($context->workingDirectory); // will print the directory of the castor.php file

    $context = $context->withWorkingDirectory('/tmp'); // will create a new context where the current directory is /tmp
    run('pwd', context: $context); // will print "/tmp"
}
```

### The working directory

By default, only `run()` executes in the working directory of the context.
Everything else, `fs()`, `finder()` and the raw PHP functions such as `mkdir()`
or `file_get_contents()`, resolves relative paths from the directory you called
`castor` from.

You can opt in to a single, consistent behavior by defining a constant at the top
of your `castor.php` file:

```php
defined('CASTOR_USE_CHDIR') || define('CASTOR_USE_CHDIR', true);
```

The guard matters as soon as several `castor.php` files run in the same process:
a mounted project, an imported file or a `composer://` package may define the
constant too, and a second bare `define()` would raise
`Constant CASTOR_USE_CHDIR already defined`.

Castor then changes the current directory of its own process to the working
directory of the context, so relative paths mean the same thing everywhere,
whatever directory you called `castor` from. This also applies while a
`with(workingDirectory: ...)` block runs, and the previous directory is restored
when it ends:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\io;
use function Castor\with;

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    io()->writeln(getcwd()); // the directory of the castor.php file

    with(static function () {
        io()->writeln(getcwd()); // "/tmp"
        file_put_contents('foo.txt', 'bar'); // writes "/tmp/foo.txt"
    }, workingDirectory: '/tmp');

    io()->writeln(getcwd()); // the directory of the castor.php file, again
}
```

> [!NOTE]
> This becomes the default in Castor 2.0. Until then, Castor emits a deprecation
> when the constant is not defined. Define it to `false` to keep the current
> behavior without the deprecation.

### The `variable()` function

Castor also provides a `variable()` function to get the value of a variable
stored in the `Context`:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\context;
use function Castor\variable;

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    $foobar = variable('foobar', 'default value');

    // Same as:
    $context = context();
    try {
        $foobar = $context['foobar'];
    } catch (\OutOfBoundsException) {
        $foobar = 'default value;
    }
}
```

### Typing the context data

Castor cannot know the shape of your context data, so `Context::$data` and
`variable()` are described by a PHPStan [type
alias](https://phpstan.org/writing-php-code/phpdoc-types#global-type-aliases)
named `ContextData`. It defaults to `array<string, mixed>`, which means
`variable()` returns `mixed` out of the box.

If you use PHPStan, you can redeclare that alias in your own `phpstan.neon` to
describe your own variables:

```neon
parameters:
    typeAliases:
        ContextData: '''
            array{
                name: string,
                production: bool,
                foo?: string,
            }
        '''
```

`variable()` then returns precise types instead of `mixed`:

```php
$name = variable('name');                // string
$production = variable('production');    // bool
$unknown = variable('unknown', 42);      // int, inferred from the default value
```

Your declaration takes precedence over the default one, so there is nothing
else to remove or disable.

> [!NOTE]
> The default alias lives in `extension.neon` at the root of the Castor
> package. It is registered automatically if you use
> [phpstan/extension-installer](https://github.com/phpstan/extension-installer).
> Otherwise, include it by hand:
>
> ```neon
> includes:
>     - vendor/jolicode/castor/extension.neon
> ```
>
> When you run Castor as a phar or as a standalone binary there is no
> `vendor/jolicode/castor` directory: declare the alias yourself, either with your
> own shape or with the permissive default `ContextData: 'array<string, mixed>'`.

## Creating a new context

You can create a new context by declaring a function with
the `Castor\Attribute\AsContext` attribute:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsContext;
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;
use Castor\Context;

use function Castor\run;

#[AsContext()]
function my_context(): Context
{
    return new Context(environment: ['FOO' => 'BAR']);
}

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    run('echo foo=$FOO');
}
```

> [!NOTE]
> If you only define one context in your project, it will be used by default for
> all tasks.
> See the next chapter to learn how to set a default context.

So when you run the `foo` task, you will get:

```console
$ castor foo
foo=BAR
```

## Working with several contexts

Defining multiple contexts can be useful to represent different environments
(e.g. `dev`, `staging`, `prod`, etc.) or different configurations (e.g. `docker`, `local`, etc.).

You can define as many contexts as you want in your project by declaring multiple
functions with the `#[AsContext]` attribute:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsContext;
use Castor\Context;

#[AsContext()]
function dev_context(): Context
{
    return new Context(environment: ['APP_ENV' => 'dev']);
}

#[AsContext()]
function test_context(): Context
{
    return new Context(environment: ['APP_ENV' => 'test']);
}
```

You can then choose which context to use when running a task by using the
`--context` option:

```bash
castor foo --context=dev_context
```

> [!TIP]
> The `-c` option is a shortcut for the `--context` option in order to make it
> easier to type.

```bash
castor foo -c dev_context
```

### Overriding the context name

You can override the context name by setting the `name` argument of the
`#[AsContext]` attribute:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsContext;
use Castor\Context;

use function Castor\run;

#[AsContext(name: 'dev')]
function dev_context(): Context
{
    return new Context(environment: ['APP_ENV' => 'dev']);
}
```

### Setting a default context

You may want to set a default context for all your tasks. You can do that by
setting the `default` argument to `true` in the `#[AsContext]` attribute:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsContext;
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;
use Castor\Context;

use function Castor\run;

#[AsContext(default: true, name: 'default')]
function default_context(): Context
{
    return new Context();
}

#[AsContext(name: 'my_context')]
function other_context(): Context
{
    return new Context(environment: ['FOO' => 'BAR']);
}

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    run('echo foo=$FOO');
}
```

By default the `foo` task will only print `foo=` as the `FOO` environment
variable is not set:

```console
$ castor foo
foo=
```

If you want to use your other context, you can use the `--context` option:

```console
$ castor foo --context=my_context
foo=BAR
```

> [!NOTE]
> You can also define the environment variable `CASTOR_CONTEXT` at runtime to
> override the default context to be used when no `--context` option is
> provided.

```bash
CASTOR_CONTEXT=my_context castor foo
```

### Using a `.castor.context` file

You can also create a `.castor.context` file at the root of your project
(next to `castor.php`) to set the context for all team members or CI runs
without touching environment variables:

```text
my_context
```

The file must contain a single line with the name of a valid context.
If the context name is unknown, Castor will log an error and fall back to
the default context.

The context selection precedence is, from highest to lowest:

1. `--context` CLI option
2. `CASTOR_CONTEXT` environment variable
3. `.castor.context` file
4. The context marked `default: true`

> [!TIP]
> The `.castor.context` file is useful when you want to commit a default
> context for your project (e.g. `production`) while still allowing each
> developer to override it locally via the `--context` flag or the
> `CASTOR_CONTEXT` environment variable. Add it to `.gitignore` if you
> want each developer to manage their own local context.

## Context features

### Failure

By default, Castor will throw an exception if the process fails. You can disable
that by using the `withAllowFailure` method:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\context;
use function Castor\run;

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    run('a_command_that_does_not_exist', context: context()->withAllowFailure());
}
```

### Working directory

By default, Castor will execute the process in the same directory as
the `castor.php` file. You can change that by using the `withWorkingDirectory`
method. It can be either a relative or an absolute path:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\context;
use function Castor\run;

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    run('pwd', context: context()->withWorkingDirectory('../')); // run the process in the parent directory of the castor.php file
    run('pwd', context: context()->withWorkingDirectory('/tmp')); // run the process in the /tmp directory
}
```

### Environment variables

By default, Castor will use the same environment variables as the current
process. You can add or override environment variables by using the
`withEnvironment()` method:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\context;
use function Castor\run;

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    run('echo $FOO', context: context()->withEnvironment(['FOO' => 'bar'])); // will print "bar"
}
```

> [!WARNING]
> The environment variables of the context are displayed, with their values,
> in the command Castor reports when a process fails, and in the verbose logs
> (`-v`). Keep secrets out of `withEnvironment()` when that output can be read
> by others, in CI logs for instance. Variables inherited from the parent
> process (exported in your shell, or loaded with `load_dot_env()`) are passed
> to the process too, but are never displayed.

### Timeout

By default, Castor allow your `run()` calls to go indefinitly.

If you want to tweak that you need to use the `withTimeout` method.

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\context;
use function Castor\run;

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    run('my-script.sh', context: context()->withTimeout(120));
}
```

This process will have a 2 minutes timeout.

### PTY & TTY

By default, Castor will use a pseudo terminal (PTY) to run the underlying process,
which allows to have nice output in most cases.
For some commands, you may want to disable the PTY and use a TTY instead. You can
do that by using the `withTty` method:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\context;
use function Castor\run;

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    run('echo "bar"', context: context()->withTty());
}
```

> [!WARNING]
> When using a TTY, the output of the command is empty in the process object
> (when using `getOutput()` or `getErrorOutput()`).

You can also disable the pty by using the `withPty` method. If `withTty`
and `withPty` are both used with `false`, the standard input will not be forwarded to
the process:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\context;
use function Castor\run;

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    run('echo "bar"', context: context()->withPty(false)->withTty(false)); // print nothing
}
```

### Trapping signals

By default, a signal sent to Castor - like the `SIGINT` triggered by a `CTRL+C` -
stops Castor itself. You can ask Castor to trap some signals and forward them to
the process it runs, with the `withTrappedSignals` method:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\context;
use function Castor\run;

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    // A CTRL+C stops the server, but not the task
    run('./my-server', context: context()->withTrappedSignals()->withAllowFailure());

    run('echo "the server has been stopped"');
}
```

Without any argument, this method traps `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM`. You can also
pass the list of signals you want to trap, like
`withTrappedSignals([\SIGINT, \SIGQUIT])`. `SIGKILL` and `SIGSTOP` cannot be
caught, and are rejected with an `InvalidArgumentException`.

See [the signals documentation](../going-further/interacting-with-castor/signals.md#trapping-signals-sent-to-castor)
for more information.

### Interactive environment

Some commands (a shell, `vim`, an interactive prompt, ...) only make sense
when Castor runs in an interactive environment. Castor auto-detects this and
exposes it via `supportsInteraction()`:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\context;
use function Castor\run;

#[AsTask()]
function shell(): void
{
    $c = context();

    if ($c->supportsInteraction()) {
        $c = $c->toInteractive();
    }

    run('bash', context: $c);
}
```

Auto-detection considers the environment **non-interactive** when:

* the `CI` environment variable is set, or
* `STDIN` is not attached to a TTY (piped input, AI agent runners, ...).

You can also force the value yourself with `withSupportsInteraction()`, for
example to flag your own AI agent runner:

```php
$c = context()->withSupportsInteraction(false);
```

Calling `toInteractive()` in a non-interactive environment throws a
`LogicException` to prevent silent hangs. If you really want to force
interactive flags anyway, pass `throwOnNonInteractiveEnv: false`:

```php
$c = context()->toInteractive(throwOnNonInteractiveEnv: false);
```

### Passing verbose arguments

Castor allow you to pass verbose arguments (like the universal `-v` option) to
the underlying process. You can do that by using the `withVerboseArguments` method:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\context;
use function Castor\run;

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    run('php bin/console do:some:task', context: context()->withVerboseArguments(['--verbose']));
}
```

By default, Castor will not pass any verbose arguments to the command. However,
if you run castor [in verbose mode](../going-further/interacting-with-castor/log.md)
(for example with `castor foo -v`), it will pass the verbose arguments you configured to this command.

Additionally, if this command fails when Castor is not in verbose mode, it will
ask you if you want to retry the command with the verbose arguments.

## Advanced usage

See [this documentation](../going-further/interacting-with-castor/advanced-context.md) for more usage about
contexts.

# Repacking your application in a new phar

You have created a Castor application, with many tasks, and you want to
distribute it as a single phar file? Castor can help you with that.

## Pre-requisites

You'll need
[box](https://github.com/box-project/box/blob/main/doc/installation.md#installation)
to create the phar. The box binary must be available in your path.

You'll also need to ensure the phar creation is allowed by your PHP
configuration. See the [PHP
documentation](https://www.php.net/manual/en/phar.configuration.php#ini.phar.readonly) to disabled
`phar.readonly`.

## Running the Repack Command

Then, run the repack command to create the new phar:

```bash
castor repack
```

> [!NOTE]
> Castor will automatically import all files in the current directory.
> So ensure to have the fewer files possible in the directory where you run the
> repack task to avoid including useless files in the phar.
<!-- -->
> [!NOTE]
> If a `box.json` file exists in your application directory,
> it will be merged with the config file used by Castor.
> None of these keys `base-path`, `main`, `alias` or `output` keys can be
> defined in your application box config.
<!-- -->
> [!CAUTION]
> If some classes are missing in your phar, it might be because they are
> excluded by castor's `box.json` file. In this case, you should override the
> default configuration with a local `box.json` file
<!-- -->
> [!NOTE]
> The Castor phar embedded in your application is downloaded from the GitHub
> releases, with the `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment variable as credentials when it
> is set (it raises the API rate limit in CI). When the
> [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) is installed and authenticated, the
> provenance of the phar is verified with `gh attestation verify`, and a phar
> without attestation is refused: pass the `--allow-unattested` option to
> embed a Castor release published before attestations existed.
<!-- -->
> [!NOTE]
> The remote packages of `castor.composer.json` are installed by the Castor
> running the command, so they are resolved against
> [the packages bundled with this version](remote-imports.md#packages-bundled-with-castor).
> When the `--castor-version` or `--castor-phar` option embeds another Castor
> version, make sure the remote packages are compatible with the packages it
> ships too.

{% include-markdown "/build/command_castor-repack.md" start="`castor:repack`\n---------------" %}

## Repack with your logo

When you repack, you can use the `--no-logo` option to hide the Castor logo.

Alternatively, you can replace the Castor logo with your own.
Use the `--logo-file` option and provide the absolute path (or a path relative
to the working directory) of a `.php` file.

This file must return a string or a closure that returns a string.
The closure will receive the application name and version as string parameters.

### Example

```php
// repack/my-logo.php

<?php

return '❤️ My LOGO ❤️';
```

```bash
castor repack --logo-file repack/my-logo.php
```

or

```php
// repack/my-complex-logo.php

<?php

return function (string $appName, string $appVersion) {
    return <<<LOGO

    ❤️ My LOGO for {$appName} in Version {$appVersion} ❤️

    LOGO;
};
```

```bash
castor repack --logo-file repack/my-complex-logo.php
```

![img.png](../../../assets/custom-logo.png)

## Going further

Packaging your Castor app as a phar simplifies distribution but requires PHP
setup on target systems.

[Castor's `compile` command](compile.md) streamlines this by embedding the phar
in a PHP binary, creating a static executable for diverse environments.

# Root file and shebang

This document explains how to make Castor to use a custom root file and
how to leverage shebang lines for direct script execution.

## Using a custom root file

By default, castor looks for a `castor.php` or  `.castor/castor.php` file in the
current working directory or one of its parents.

However, you can use another root file by using the `--castor-file` option:

```bash
castor --castor-file=path/to/your-file.php your-task
```

## Using a shebang line

Unix systems support shebang lines to execute scripts directly from the command
line, without having to prefix them with the interpreter.

The `--castor-file` option makes it possible to create a Castor file that can be
executed directly. For example, you can create a file named `my-script` with the
following content:

```php
{% include "/examples/advanced/castor-file/shebang.php" %}
```

Make sure to give execute permissions to your script:

```bash
chmod +x my-script
```

Now, you can run your script directly from the command line:

```bash
./my-script shebang-task
```

  such as stopping a task with CTRL+C or responding to other system signals.

# Handling signals

Castor can handle signals sent to the process. This is useful to gracefully
stop a task when the user presses `CTRL+C` or to handle other signals:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\io;

#[AsTask(onSignals: [\SIGUSR2 => 'onSigUsr2'])]
function foo(): void
{
    // Do something...
}

function onSigUsr2(int $signal): int|false
{
    io()->writeln("SIGUSR2 received\n");

    return false;
}
```

Return false to continue the task, or return an integer to stop the task
with this exit code.

If the task is in a namespace, you must use the fully qualified name of the function:

```php
namespace signal;

use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

#[AsTask(onSignals: [\SIGUSR2 => 'signal\onSigUsr2'])]
function foo(): void
{
    // Do something...
}

function onSigUsr2(int $signal): int|false
{
    io()->writeln('SIGUSR2 received');

    return false;
}
```

## Trapping signals sent to Castor

By default, a signal sent to Castor - like the `SIGINT` triggered by a `CTRL+C` -
interrupts Castor itself, and the task is not executed any further.

If you want to stop only the process currently running, and let the task
continue, you can ask the context to trap the signals with the
`withTrappedSignals()` method. When Castor receives one of these signals while
running a process, it forwards it to that process instead of being interrupted:

```php
{% include "/examples/advanced/signal/trap.php" start="<?php\n\nnamespace signal;\n\n" %}
```

Without any argument, `withTrappedSignals()` traps `SIGINT` and `SIGTERM`. You
can trap other signals by passing the list you want:

```php
use Castor\Attribute\AsTask;

use function Castor\context;
use function Castor\run;

#[AsTask()]
function foo(): void
{
    run('./my-server', context: context()->withTrappedSignals([\SIGINT, \SIGQUIT]));
}
```

`SIGKILL` and `SIGSTOP` cannot be caught by a process: passing one of them to
`withTrappedSignals()` throws an `InvalidArgumentException`.

Since the process is stopped by a signal, it exits with a non-zero exit code
(`130` for a `SIGINT`, `143` for a `SIGTERM`, ...). As for any other failure,
Castor throws a `ProcessFailedException`, unless you use the
[`withAllowFailure()`](../../getting-started/context.md#failure) method.

As the trap is only installed while a process is running, a signal received
between two `run()` calls keeps its usual behavior and stops Castor.

Signals are forwarded to the process started by Castor only, not to the
processes this one may have started itself. Note also that a `CTRL+C` is sent by
the terminal to every process of the foreground process group, so the process
usually receives it directly too.

### Combining a trap with the `onSignals` handlers

A trapped signal is consumed by Castor: while the process is running, the
`onSignals` handler of the task is not called for this signal, as the signal is
meant for the process. Once the process is finished, the trap is released and
the handler of the task gets the signals again:

```php
{% include "/examples/advanced/signal/trap_with_on_signals.php" start="<?php\n\nnamespace signal;\n\n" %}
```

This example sends the signals to itself, but hitting `CTRL+C` once while the
process runs, then once after it, has the same effect and outputs:

```text
The process has been stopped with the exit code 130
SIGINT received by the task itself
And Castor is still running!
```

> [!WARNING]
> Trapping signals requires the `pcntl` extension. When it is not available -
> on Windows, for instance - the signals are not trapped, and Castor keeps its
> default behavior.

<?php

namespace Castor\Console;

use Castor\Exception\ProblemException;
use Castor\Helper\PlatformHelper;
use Castor\Kernel;
use Castor\Runner\ProcessRunner;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Application as SymfonyApplication;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Command\Command;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Exception\CommandNotFoundException;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Formatter\OutputFormatter;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\InputDefinition;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\InputInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\InputOption;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Output\OutputInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Style\SymfonyStyle;
use Symfony\Component\DependencyInjection\Attribute\Autowire;
use Symfony\Component\Process\Exception\ProcessFailedException;

/** @internal */
class Application extends SymfonyApplication
{
    public const NAME = 'castor';
    public const VERSION = 'v1.8.1';
    public const HIDE_LOGO = false;
    public const EXTERNAL_LOGO = '';

    private Command $command;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly Kernel $kernel,
        #[Autowire(lazy: true)]
        private readonly SymfonyStyle $io,
        #[Autowire(lazy: true)]
        private readonly ProcessRunner $processRunner,
        #[Autowire('%test%')]
        public readonly bool $test,
        public readonly bool $hasCastorFile,
    ) {
        parent::__construct(static::NAME, static::VERSION);
    }

    /**
     * Whether this build comes from a commit that is not a release: the phar
     * build then sets a version like "v1.7.0-14-g4531440".
     */
    public static function isSnapshot(): bool
    {
        return str_contains(self::VERSION, '-');
    }

    /**
     * @return ($allowNull is true ? ?Command : Command)
     */
    public function getCommand(bool $allowNull = false): ?Command
    {
        return $this->command ?? ($allowNull ? null : throw new \LogicException('Command not available yet.'));
    }

    public function doRun(InputInterface $input, OutputInterface $output): int
    {
        if ($input->hasParameterOption(['--version', '-V'], true)) {
            // skip the boot process
            return parent::doRun($input, $output);
        }

        $this->kernel->init($input, $output);

        try {
            return parent::doRun($input, $output);
        } catch (CommandNotFoundException $e) {
            if (!$this->hasCastorFile) {
                $this->io->warning('Could not find root "castor.php" file. Did you run castor in the right directory?');
            }

            throw $e;
        }
    }

    public function getHelp(): string
    {
        // @phpstan-ignore if.alwaysFalse
        if (self::HIDE_LOGO) {
            return parent::getHelp();
        }

        return $this->getLogo() . parent::getHelp();
    }

    public function renderThrowable(\Throwable $e, OutputInterface $output): void
    {
        if (!$output->isVerbose()) {
            $this->enhanceException($e);

            if ($e instanceof ProblemException) {
                $this->io->error($e->getMessage());

                return;
            }

            if ($e instanceof ProcessFailedException) {
                $process = $e->getProcess();
                $runnable = $this->processRunner->buildRunnableCommand($process);

                $this->io->writeln(\sprintf('<comment>%s</comment>', OutputFormatter::escape(\sprintf('In %s line %s:', basename($e->getFile()) ?: 'n/a', $e->getLine() ?: 'n/a'))));
                $this->io->error('The following process did not finish successfully (exit code ' . $process->getExitCode() . '):');
                $this->io->writeln("<fg=yellow>{$runnable}</>");
                $this->io->newLine();

                $this->io->comment('Re-run the command with the <fg=yellow>-v</> option to see more details.');

                return;
            }
        }

        parent::renderThrowable($e, $output);
    }

    protected function doRunCommand(Command $command, InputInterface $input, OutputInterface $output): int
    {
        $this->command = $command;

        return parent::doRunCommand($command, $input, $output);
    }

    protected function getDefaultInputDefinition(): InputDefinition
    {
        $definition = parent::getDefaultInputDefinition();

        $definition->addOption(
            new InputOption(
                'no-remote',
                null,
                InputOption::VALUE_NONE,
                'Skip the import of all remote remote packages',
            )
        );

        $definition->addOption(
            new InputOption(
                'update-remotes',
                null,
                InputOption::VALUE_NONE,
                'Force the update of remote packages',
            )
        );

        $definition->addOption(
            new InputOption(
                'castor-file',
                null,
                InputOption::VALUE_OPTIONAL,
                'Specify an alternative castor file to use instead of the default "castor.php"',
            )
        );

        return $definition;
    }

    private function enhanceException(\Throwable $exception): void
    {
        if ($exception instanceof \Error) {
            return;
        }

        $castorDirs = [
            \dirname(__DIR__, 1),
            \dirname(__DIR__, 2) . \DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR . 'vendor',
            \dirname(__DIR__, 2) . \DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR . 'bin',
            // Useful for the phar, or static binary
            $_SERVER['SCRIPT_NAME'],
        ];

        foreach ($exception->getTrace() as $frame) {
            if (!\array_key_exists('file', $frame) || !\array_key_exists('line', $frame)) {
                continue;
            }

            foreach ($castorDirs as $dir) {
                if (str_starts_with($frame['file'], (string) $dir)) {
                    continue 2;
                }
            }

            new \ReflectionProperty(\Exception::class, 'file')->setValue($exception, $frame['file']);
            new \ReflectionProperty(\Exception::class, 'line')->setValue($exception, $frame['line']);

namespace Castor\Console;

use Castor\Helper\PathHelper;
use Castor\Kernel;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Application as SymfonyApplication;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\ArgvInput;
use Symfony\Component\DependencyInjection\Attribute\Exclude;
use Symfony\Component\ErrorHandler\ErrorHandler;
use Symfony\Component\Filesystem\Path;
use Symfony\Component\VarDumper\Caster\StubCaster;
use Symfony\Component\VarDumper\Cloner\AbstractCloner;
use Symfony\Contracts\EventDispatcher\Event;

/** @internal */
#[Exclude]
class ApplicationFactory
{
    public static function create(): SymfonyApplication
    {
        $errorHandler = self::configureDebug();

        if (class_exists(\RepackedApplication::class)) {
            $rootDir = \RepackedApplication::ROOT_DIR;
            $repacked = true;
        } else {
            $repacked = false;
        }

        $hasCastorFile = true;
        $castorFilePath = null;

        if (!$repacked) {
            // Try to see if we want to load a different castor file
            $castorFile = new ArgvInput()->getParameterOption('--castor-file', null);

            if ($castorFile) {
                $rootDir = \dirname($castorFile);
                $castorFilePath = Path::makeRelative($castorFile, $rootDir);
            } else {
                try {
                    $rootDir = PathHelper::getRoot();
                } catch (\RuntimeException $e) {
                    $rootDir = getcwd();
                    $hasCastorFile = false;
                }
            }
        }

        // Once the process moves to the working directory of the context, a relative root would
        // resolve against the wrong directory. When there is no current directory at all, which
        // happens when the one the shell sits in has been deleted, there is nothing to resolve
        // it against, so leave it alone rather than throw before anything else runs.
        if (!$repacked && false !== ($cwd = getcwd())) {
            $rootDir = Path::makeAbsolute((string) $rootDir, $cwd);
        }

        $kernel = new Kernel('dev', true, $rootDir, $hasCastorFile, $castorFilePath, $repacked);
        $kernel->boot();

        $container = $kernel->getContainer();
        $container->set(ErrorHandler::class, $errorHandler);

        // @phpstan-ignore-next-line
        return $container->get(Application::class);
    }

    private static function configureDebug(): ErrorHandler
    {
        $errorHandler = ErrorHandler::register();

        AbstractCloner::$defaultCasters[Application::class] = StubCaster::cutInternals(...);
        AbstractCloner::$defaultCasters[Event::class] = StubCaster::cutInternals(...);

        return $errorHandler;
    }
}

namespace Castor\Console\Command;

use Castor\Console\Input\GetRawTokenTrait;
use Castor\Console\Output\VerbosityLevel;
use Castor\ContextRegistry;
use Castor\Exception\ProblemException;
use Castor\Import\Remote\Composer;
use Castor\Runner\PhpRunner;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Attribute\AsCommand;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Command\Command;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\InputArgument;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\InputInterface;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\InputOption;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Output\OutputInterface;
use Symfony\Component\DependencyInjection\Attribute\Autowire;
use Symfony\Component\Filesystem\Filesystem;

/** @internal */
#[AsCommand(
    name: 'castor:execute',
    description: 'Execute a remote task from a packagist directory',
    aliases: ['execute'],
)]
final class ExecuteCommand extends Command
{
    use GetRawTokenTrait;

    public function __construct(
        #[Autowire(lazy: true)]
        private readonly Composer $composer,
        private readonly Filesystem $filesystem,
        private readonly PhpRunner $phpRunner,
        private readonly ContextRegistry $contextRegistry,
        private readonly string $cacheDir,
    ) {
        parent::__construct();
    }

    protected function configure(): void
    {
        $this
            ->addOption('deps', 'd', InputOption::VALUE_IS_ARRAY | InputOption::VALUE_REQUIRED, 'Additional dependencies to install')
            ->addArgument('package', InputArgument::REQUIRED, 'Package to execute in the format "vendor/package:version@binary" or "vendor/package@binary" or "vendor/package"')
            ->ignoreValidationErrors()
        ;
    }

    protected function execute(InputInterface $input, OutputInterface $output): int
    {
        // Create temporary directory
        $tmpDir = tempnam($this->cacheDir, 'castor-exec-');

        if (!$tmpDir) {
            throw new \RuntimeException('Could not create temporary directory');
        }

        unlink($tmpDir);

        // format of execute is "vendor/package:version@binary"
        /** @var string[] $deps */
        $deps = $input->getOption('deps') ?? [];
        $name = $input->getArgument('package');
        $nameSplitted = explode('@', $name);

        if (\count($nameSplitted) >= 2) {
            $deps[] = $nameSplitted[0];
            $binary = $nameSplitted[1];
        } else {
            $deps[] = $name;
            $binary = null;
        }

        $composerJsonPath = $tmpDir . '/composer.json';
        $vendorDirectory = $tmpDir . '/vendor';
        $binaryDirectory = $tmpDir . '/bin';
        $tokens = $this->getRawTokens($input, false);

        $args = [];
        $foundPackageName = false;

        foreach ($tokens as $token) {
            if ($foundPackageName) {
                $args[] = $token;
            } else {
                if ($token === $name) {
                    $foundPackageName = true;
                }
            }
        }

        try {
            $this->filesystem->mkdir($tmpDir, 0o755);
            /** @var list<string> $composerArgs */
            $composerArgs = ['require', ...$deps, '--no-interaction'];
            $verbosityLevel = VerbosityLevel::fromSymfonyOutput($output);
            if (!$verbosityLevel->isVerbose()) {
                $composerArgs[] = '--quiet';
            }
            // The package runs in its own PHP process, so it can bring any
            // version of the packages bundled with Castor
            $this->composer->run($composerJsonPath, $vendorDirectory, $composerArgs, $output, $input->isInteractive(), $binaryDirectory, useBundledPackages: false);

            if (null === $binary) {
                // / Get first binary declared in the package if none was specified
                $lockFilePath = $tmpDir . '/composer.lock';
                $lockContent = json_decode(file_get_contents($lockFilePath) ?: '{}', true);

                $foundPackage = [];

                foreach ($lockContent['packages'] as $package) {
                    if ($package['name'] === $nameSplitted[0]) {
                        $foundPackage = $package;

                        break;
                    }
                }

                $binary = $foundPackage['bin'][0] ?? null;
                $binary = $binary ? basename($binary) : null;

                if (null === $binary) {
                    throw new ProblemException("No binary found for package '{$nameSplitted[0]}': you must use a package with a vendor binary, see \nhttps://getcomposer.org/doc/articles/vendor-binaries.md for more information");
                }
            }

            $context = $this->contextRegistry->getCurrentContext()->withAllowFailure();

            // By default the run command will use the directory of the root castor.php file
            // but this command should be executed in the same directory as where it was launched,
            // which is not getcwd() anymore once the process followed the context
            if (false !== ($workingDir = $this->contextRegistry->getOriginalWorkingDirectory())) {
                $context = $context->withWorkingDirectory($workingDir);
            }

            return $this->phpRunner->run($binaryDirectory . '/' . $binary, $args, $context)->wait();
        } finally {
            $this->filesystem->remove($tmpDir);
        }
    }
}
